0.title: Aethari Order
0.text:
# Aethari Order

The Aethari Order, also known as the Order of the Aethari, and the New Aethari Order under Aethari Master Tavin Vossar, was a noble monastic and nontheistic religious order united in their devotion to the light side of the Flux. They served as mediators, warriors, and with teaching and exploratory efforts. With a history dating back thousands of years before the rise of the Dominion of Astra, the Aethari Knights —noted for their lumeblades and natural ability to harness the powers of the Flux —stood as the guardians of peace and justice in the Concord of Worlds. The Order was originally established on Teyra in the Uncharted Expanse. In later years, the Aethari Grand Temple on the Core World Valcora served as the hub of all Aethari activity in the galaxy. The Temple was also a training school for fledglings and Novitiates, who learned the ways of the Flux under the supervision of Aethari Masters, twelve of whom were elected to serve on the Aethari High Council —the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master, who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Aethari Master, and the Master of the Order, who served as the Council's appointed leader. The Aethari Code governed the Order's way of life; therefore, every Aethari was duty-bound to observe and uphold the Code or else risk expulsion from the Order.

1.title: Aethari Order
1.text: The emergence of the Morrak Order was the result of a schism that fractured Aethari unity, dividing the Order between the Aethari who remained faithful to the light and a group of renegades that followed a rogue Aethari into exile for exploring the dark side of the Flux. Thenceforth, the Aethari and Morrak warred with each other for centuries. Although the last conflict concluded with the fall of the Old Concord, the ancient Morrak all but perished as well, allowing a new Concord of Worlds to rise under the protection of the Aethari Order. Unknown to the Aethari, however, the Morrak endured in secret for a millennium, beginning with Xarn Kesh, the sole-surviving Dark Lord of the Morrak who reformed the Morrak way by creating the Law of Pairs —a rule limiting the Morrak Order's ranks to two members: a Morrak Master to embody the power of the dark side, and a Morrak apprentice to covet that power. While the Aethari and Concord moved on, their ancient wars with the Morrak fading from memory, Kesh's legacy spawned a lineage of Morrak Lords that culminated in the rise of Xarn Nocturne approximately three decades before the Battle of Ostara.

2.title: Aethari Order
2.text: During the final decades of the Concord, the Aethari Order vowed allegiance to the Galactic Assembly as the galaxy was beset by political instability and social unrest which, in turn, created a secessionist crisis that ultimately resulted in the formation of the Coalition of Free Systems. Lacking the sufficient manpower needed to protect the galaxy, the Aethari became commanders and generals in the newly-formed Grand Army of the Concord. For roughly three years they commanded armies of replicant troopers in a conflict known as the Mirror Wars, engaging the Confederacy's battle droid forces led by Count Varkon —a former Aethari Master who became a Morrak Lord —and the cybernetic warlord General Kragg. Though the Aethari fought to preserve the Concord, the government they served was secretly taken over by Nocturne who, as Delegate Aldus Crayle of Lirael, rose to power in the Assembly and became the last Supreme Chancellor of the Concord. The Aethari were unknowingly being deceived by the Morrak.

3.title: Aethari Order
3.text: The Chancellor's deceptions and machinations culminated in the execution of Directive Nine, a secret protocol that forcibly turned the Aethari's replicant soldiers against them, leading to an all but total extermination of the Aethari Order. With most of the Aethari eliminated, Nocturne supplanted a thousand years of democracy with a new government known as the Dominion of Astra. In addition, Nocturne succeeded in manipulating Kaelen Vossar —the prophesied Foretold One who was destined to bring balance to the Flux by destroying the Morrak—to betray the Aethari and join the dark side, with Nocturne renaming him Xarn Velgor. As a Morrak Lord, the former Aethari Knight served the self-proclaimed Galactic Sovereign by hunting down the few surviving Aethari, who had gone into hiding across the galaxy. In spite of the Morrak's efforts, however, the Aethari continued to endure. Within a generation of the Dominion's rise to power, Odrin Halvane and Morro —both of whom survived the initial purge of the Order—trained Velgor's son, Tavin Vossar, in the Aethari arts. Tavin would later redeem his father, causing the redeemed Kaelen Vossar to return to the light and fulfill his destiny as the Foretold One, destroying both himself and his Master during the Battle of Sylvar.

4.title: Aethari Order
4.text:
The Dominion dissolved into various remnants as a result of their defeat in the Sundering War, allowing the League to Restore the Concord to rise as the New Concord. Under the new era, Tavin Vossar endeavored to rebuild the Order by training a new generation of Aethari. Among Vossar's students was his nephew, Corin Rennick, the son of his twin sister, Princess Ilsa Marrow, and the famed smuggler Dace Rennick. Corin, however, was seduced by the dark side of the Flux at the coaxing of Gorrath, an enigmatic figure who spearheaded the Dominion-inspired Iron Mandate. Tavin confronted and frightened Corin, who fought back and fled. As a result, Corin adopted the name and persona of Vael Durn, a Iron Mandate warlord and master of the Knights of Durn.

The new generation was betrayed and destroyed by Durn, who left the Aethari training temple burning by the time Vossar recovered from the attack. Feeling responsible for Corin's fall and the massacre of his apprentices, he went into exile and disappeared from the galaxy, leaving only traces of his location on a star map. The Iron Mandate and the Ember Front both sought to acquire the map, but ultimately it was the latter that succeeded due to the actions of the Saddar scavenger Nira. She followed the map to the planet Teyra, where the last Aethari had taken refuge in the first Aethari Temple.

5.title: Aethari Order
5.text: Vossar, stricken by grief and believing his return would only cause more problems, was reluctant to train Nira or another generation of Aethari. However, the last Aethari eventually returned to the fight, buying time for the Ember Front to escape the siege of Saltmere led by Vael Durn, who became the new Supreme Leader after killing his master, Gorrath. Vossar became one with the Flux after exerting a great amount of energy to project himself across the galaxy to face his fallen nephew, but not before acknowledging that he would not be the last Aethari. His heroic tale spread across the galaxy, inspiring others and giving hope in a time of rising darkness.

6.title: Ardel Strosk
6.text:
# Ardel Strosk

Ardel Strosk, a Flux-sensitive human male, was a venerable if maverick Aethari Master who lived during the last years of the Concord Era. He was a wise and well-respected member of the Aethari Order, and was offered a seat on the Aethari Council, but chose to reject and follow his own path. Adhering to a philosophy centered around the Living Flux, Strosk strove to follow the will of the Flux even when his actions conflicted with the wishes of the High Council. After encountering Kaelen Vossar, Strosk brought him to the Aethari Temple on Valcora, convinced he had found the Foretold One. His dying wish was for Vossar to become a Aethari and ultimately restore balance to the Flux.

7.title: Ardel Strosk
7.text: Born on the Core World Valcora, the capital of the Concord of Worlds around 80 BVC, Strosk learned the ways of the Flux as the Novitiate of Aethari Master Varkon before ultimately attaining the rank of Aethari Knight in around 58 BVC. In 44 BVC he would go on to take an apprentice of his own, Odrin Halvane, who adhered to the principles of the Aethari Code more than his own master. Although their relationship was sometimes tough, the two Aethari overcame early difficulties during a mission to Pijal, which concluded in Strosk turning down a request to join the Aethari Council to continue teaching his apprentice. When the Mercantile Combine initiated a blockade of the Middle Reach planet Lirael in 32 BVC, Strosk and Halvane were dispatched to resolve the crisis at the request of Supreme Chancellor Aurel Esteven. Influenced by the mysterious Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, the Federation launched a full-scale invasion of Lirael, forcing the Aethari to rescue Queen Selene Corvane after the fall of Elmira.

8.title: Ardel Strosk
8.text: During their journey to the galactic capital, the group was forced to land on the Far Reach planet Drysa where Strosk encountered a young slave named Kaelen Vossar. Using a scientific method to gauge the boy's potential, he learned that Vossar had more lumicytes in his blood than any Flux-sensitive in galactic history, including Grand Master Morro. The revelation that he was the result of a miracle birth—a child born of a mother, but had no father —confirmed Strosk's suspicion that Vossar was the Foretold One destined to restore balance to the Flux. Before departing the desert world with Vossar, Strosk was confronted by Nocturne' Morrak apprentice Xarn Skarr. Although their duel was brief, it convinced Strosk that the Morrak had returned after a millennium of silence.

9.title: Ardel Strosk
9.text: At the Temple, Strosk was adamant that Vossar was the Foretold One and should, therefore, be inducted into the Aethari Order. However, having inspected Vossar for themselves, the High Council deemed him too old, emotional, and dangerously full of fear and anger. Strosk saw their decision as a temporary setback, but the need to resolve the situation on Queen Corvane's homeworld forced him to set aside his plans for Vossar. During the Battle of Lirael, Strosk and Halvane confronted Xarn Skarr together. While they initially managed to fend off the Morrak Lord's attacks, master and apprentice were eventually separated during the lumeblade duel, resulting in Strosk sustaining a mortal injury. Rushing to his master's aid, Halvane fought and ultimately defeated the Dathomirian Morrak, but could not save Strosk. With his last breath, Strosk made Halvane promise that he would take Vossar as his apprentice. Having secured Halvane's word, Strosk became one with the Flux, dying with the certainty that he had found the prophesied Foretold One.

10.title: Ardel Strosk
10.text:
## Biography

### Early life

Ardel Strosk was a male human born on the galactic capital of Valcora circa 80 BVC. He was taken to the Aethari Temple as a boy for training by the Aethari Order and was assigned to the Heliost Clan where he learned lumeblade combat from Aethari Master Tera Sinube.

When Strosk was twelve years old, he was assigned as a Novitiate to Aethari Master Varkon, from whom he learned the ways of the Flux. He'd spent his last night in the fledglings' crèche laughing with his friends, imagining all the adventures he would have as a Novitiate, and practicing with his lumeblade in the sparring room until Master Yaddle ordered him to bed.

When the future Aethari Master Eno Cordova first joined the Aethari Order, he became close friends with Strosk, who helped Cordova learn about and get used to Valcora.

11.title: Ardel Strosk
11.text:
### Apprentice to Varkon

Around 68 BVC, when a twelve-year-old Strosk presented himself to his new Master in Varkon's quarters, Varkon observed that Strosk was frightened. After a moment of silence, and with pressing from Varkon, Strosk confessed that he was. When asked why, after looking into himself through the fear, Strosk answered that he was not afraid of Varkon, but of not becoming a Aethari, that he was afraid of failing and of not being worthy. Varkon then summarized it as Strosk being afraid of himself, of a future not being the one he wanted. Strosk confirmed it, fearing that Varkon would reject him for his cowardice. Varkon instead said that it was very wise, surprising Strosk. Smiling, Varkon explained that most Novitiates would deny their fear, and even if they admitted it, they would not have Strosk's self-knowledge. Varkon further praised Strosk for his honesty, insight, and intelligence.

12.title: Ardel Strosk
12.text: To help Strosk understand the Aethari Temple more completely, Varkon then took him throughout most of the Temple, including the Novitiates' sparring dojo, a dojo where Aethari Knights trained, and the Great Assembly Room. Strosk also saw the various meditation chambers, which he didn't find as exciting, but still interesting. On the other hand, Strosk spent long minutes in the arboretum, wandering through the trees, ferns, and flowers of a thousand different worlds. Their last stop was the Aethari Archives, where they examined memory prisms of various eras, not to study them, but simply for Strosk to learn his way around. While doing so, an ancient memory prism, more ancient and of a different shape than the rest, caught Strosk's eye. When he questioned his Master about it, he was shocked by the expression on Varkon's face, almost as if he considered it an enemy. Varkon answered that it was a memory prism of Aethari prophecies. Strosk asked if there are Aethari prophets, to which Varkon replied not any longer. He explained to Strosk that the mystics sought undue knowledge of the future, which led them down dangerous paths. The dark side often tempted those drawn too deeply into them. Varkon then finished by saying that is why the Aethari study prophecy no longer, then turned to leave, which meant Strosk had to follow. Strosk then asked Varkon if just wanting to know the future can lead to the dark side. Varkon replied that it takes more than that. This was Ardel's first encounter with the memory prism of prophecies, and it would not be the last.

13.title: Aurite crystal
13.text:
# Aurite crystal

A aurite crystal, simply known as a aurite and described as a lumeblade crystal or the living crystal, was a rare, Flux-attuned crystal that grew naturally and was found on various planets across the galaxy. Known in ancient times as a kaiburr crystal, it was used by both the Aethari and the Morrak in the construction of their lumeblades. As part of their Aethari training, fledglings were sent to the Crystal Cave of the ice planet of Ilum to seek their own lumeblade crystals. The crystal's mix of unique luster was called "the water of the aurite" by the Aethari. There were also larger, rarer crystals of great power and that, according to legends, were used at the heart of ancient superweapons by the Morrak.

14.title: Aurite crystal
14.text:
## Description

Aurite crystals were Flux-attuned crystals that grew rarely but throughout the galaxy, with some areas having a greater abundance than others. The crystals concentrated energy in a unique manner through the Flux, resonating with it. The crystals exhibited a sort of "collective consciousness," verging on sentience, and could non-verbally communicate with both one another and living beings. Some theorized that the permutations in the aurite lattice were comparable to emotional shifts in a sentient being. According to superstition, the aurite's secrets could only be unlocked by facing in a certain direction at dawn or by watching mist rise on specific remote worlds. A Aethari once called the aurite a somnolent stone that needed to be woken up to be used, requiring care to not insult the crystal.

15.title: Aurite crystal
15.text: Internally, aurite crystals were composed of both organic and inorganic matter. They were stable at temperatures and pressures found in the cores of large stars, and were thus impervious to fire and resistant to hammering, and noted for their intricate patterns. Aurite crystals were sturdy enough to survive the violent explosion of a lumeblade's power grid, such as those caused by accidentally inverting the emitter matrix during the weapon's assembly. Aurite crystals would not warm a sheath or a towel or any inanimate object, responding only to life, including plant life. If an individual were to wrap their hand around a crystal, the crystal would warm, but not change in temperature. Many scientists believed that aurite crystals could shift their shape depending on ambient energies. The crystals grew in an organized way, adding to their prismatic structure one piece at a time. They had no discernible lifespan, and thus could be found from sizes as small as a fingernail to gigantic proportions. All kybers were attuned to the Flux regardless of their size. Incorrectly pumping laser energy into the crystals weakened their lattices in the same way living cells were affected by radiation.

16.title: Aurite crystal
16.text: True kybers were only found in veins of pure kyberite. If the crystal contained impurities, it was regarded as a false aurite. Ranite was closely related to kyberite, but was denser and tougher, and did not contain aurite crystals. Crystals were typically brought to the surface of planets by movements along fault lines, exhumed from the high temperatures and pressure conditions in which they formed. The crystals could be mined from secondary deposits in streams, perhaps following long transport, owing to their mechanical and chemical resilience. Alternately, they could be found in their primary, in situ positions, having grown into free space on the walls of lava tubes, caves, fault zones, and within veins of kyberite.

17.title: Aurite crystal
17.text: Aurite crystals were most notably found in Ilum's Crystal Cave. They were a critical component in the construction of lumeblades, focusing energy into the weapon's distinct plasma blade. The crystals shared a special relationship with the Aethari for tens of thousands of years, and welcomed them to hear their song and learn their lessons. Aethari fledglings traveled to the ice caves to harvest their own crystals, which they then used to build their lumeblades. The Flux guided their selection, finding a crystal that matched them as Aethari. To those not meant to receive it, the crystal was cold to the touch, but those the crystal chose would hear its " music " and "harmony," becoming attracted to it. Crystals lacked color before they were chosen by a Aethari. Once chosen, most lumeblades became blue or green, though other shades were created in some instances, most notably Torvin Kell's purple blade, the yellow blades of the Aethari Temple Guards, the black Darksaber, and Baylan Skoll's orange lumeblade. The resulting crystal and blade color was decided through shifting to match the nature of the bonded owner. It was possible to alter the angle or frequency of aurite crystals or lumeblade blades, which allowed the colors of blades to be changed. This was done by Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar to his former Novitiate's lumeblades.

18.title: Aurite crystal
18.text:
Aurite crystals were inherently filled with " light side energy," and resisted any effort by dark-side practitioners to corrupt them, with one crystal in particular, that belonged to the Aethari Master Kirak Infil'a, subjecting Xarn Velgor to intense visions after he attempted to corrupt the crystal using the dark-side of the Flux. This process caused the crystal to " bleed," as if it were a living organism, resulting in the distinctive red or crimson-bladed lumeblades synonymous with the Morrak. It was possible to "heal" a corrupted aurite crystal. The information on how to heal a aurite crystal was found in the Chronicles of Brus-Bu. One instance of purifying a corrupted aurite crystal was when Lirra Sef purified the two crystals she retrieved from the Sixth Brother's lumeblade following his defeat. In this case, the crystals turned white.

The crystals were noted for their unmatched ability to channel energy and generate enormous returns. To this end, numerous individuals attempted to make synthetic aurite crystals, though their artificial nature made them highly unstable and explosive. If a crystal was subjected to forceful attempts to study it or harness its power, it would "flee" such attempts, hindering those that sought to use it against its will. Furthermore, those that worked in proximity to them would experience headaches and a loss of sleep, becoming incessantly fanatic and fixated over the crystal in the process.

19.title: Aurite crystal
19.text: For centuries, the Aethari cut and faceted the kybers to eliminate occlusions and intensify their power yield. Orrin Halden theorized that larger crystals needed to be faceted, not only to eliminate these occlusions, but also to minimize diffraction resulting from the introduction of energy from a lasing medium. With proper faceting, the pulse of energy released by the crystal could be greatly amplified and, with the help of containment devices, or be directed into a collimating beam of incredible power, as was used on the VC-1 battle station. Orrin Halden also theorized that increased energy yield could be further attained by forcing what the Aethari called the "day and night" lattices of the Flux to realign. By realigning the crystals' lattices along the dark or nighttime axis of the Flux, Orrin postulated that it could allow for greater control over the crystal's tendency to diffract. Thus, technology could be used to force the crystals to obey their masters. The abundant yield could then be siphoned off, contained, and used as enriched energy. Without containment, the yield could result in a catastrophic event, capable of wiping out a large population center.

20.title: Battle of Kryvel
20.text:
# Battle of Kryvel

The Battle of Kryvel, also known as the defense of Frostpoint Base, was a major battle fought in 3 AVC and was, often times, considered a major victory for the Dominion of Astra and the single worst battlefield defeat suffered by the Free League during the Sundering War. The battle was an Dominion invasion led by Xarn Velgor, aimed at destroying the Free League's Frostpoint Base hidden on the remote ice world Kryvel and capturing Tavin Vossar. The base's location was discovered when a Viper probe droid, deployed by Xarn Velgor's Death Squadron, landed on the planet - prompting the Insurgents to begin an evacuation of Kryvel.

The Dominion attack force consisted of primarily Strider walkers, commanded by General Maximilian Harlan. His army was tasked with destroying Frostpoint Base's main power generator to allow orbital bombardment of the planet and for Xarn Velgor to arrive and lead ground forces into the base. Spearheading the defense of the generator were the T-47 airspeeders of Rogue Squadron, commanded by Tavin Vossar, the pilot renowned for destroying the first Void Core. However, the snowspeeders did not have the necessary firepower to bring down the walkers, so Vossar suggested an alternative tactic to trip the walkers with the tow cables issued to every snowspeeder.

21.title: Battle of Kryvel
21.text: Despite the efforts by Rogue Squadron, the power generator was eventually destroyed by Harlan' main Strider. The remaining base personnel proceeded to evacuate, as the Ninth Legion, led by Xarn Velgor, entered the base. The overwhelming Dominion invasion forced the Insurgency to scatter their fleet across the galaxy, leading to a multitude of scattered skirmishes across the galaxy before the Dominion's sudden and crushing defeat at the Battle of Sylvar.

22.title: Battle of Kryvel
22.text:
## Prelude

Following the Free League's major victory at Ostara, the Insurgency abandoned its base on Ostara IV and began searching the galaxy for new possible bases of operation, considering worlds, such as Daxan Beta and Insk. They also attempted to set up base at Saltmere. In the subsequent three and a half years of conflict, General Jan Harlow ordered a mission to find a base for the High Command, drawing up a list of potential planets, which included Kryvel. During that mission, an Free League Special Forces soldier named Purpruff traveled to the planet of Kryvel in the Velisk sector and filed a report on it. Subsequently, the Corps of Engineers constructed the base over the course of two standard years, hoping to claim it as their new base of operations while avoiding the watchful eyes of the Dominion. The base was inhabited for less than a month before the battle took place.

23.title: Battle of Kryvel
23.text: Following the defeat of the Dominion three and a half years earlier at the Battle of Ostara, the Free League suffered from relentless Dominion attacks during the Middle Reach Retreat. Rumors of a Insurgent base, circulated throughout the Insurgency, though only a few in the League actually knew concrete details of its existence. Insurgent troopers at Frostpoint Base, far-distanced from the disastrous Insurgent tactical situation in the Mid and Far Reach Territories, actually had access to better equipment and training than Insurgent soldiers throughout the rest of the galaxy. The Dominion began to intensify its search for the Insurgent base after the ambush of a rebel convoy at Derra. As part of Project Swarm, the Dominion sent Viper probe droids to search for the rebel base throughout the galaxy. Doctor Chelli Lona Aphra heavily set back the Dominion's efforts to find Frostpoint Base when, by hacking into Velgor's armor while the Morrak Lord was weakened in the Martyrium of Frozen Tears, she had numerous probe droid records deleted or altered. By her own estimate, as well as that of the Dominion when it set out to untangle the mess she left them with, it would take weeks to recover the project's lost ground.

24.title: Battle of Kryvel
24.text:
Shortly before the battle, a strategy conference was held at the base after the arrival of several transports arrived, which were rumored to carry Princess Ilsa Marrow, General Carlist Hallorin, Commander Beryl Chiffonage, a Pelari spy, and several other members of League Command. The conference's main briefing was from defected Dominion governor Everi Chalis who had been extracted from Haidoral Prime by the 61st Mobile Infantry under Captain Micha Evon. Chalis offered substantial information about the inner-workings of the "Dominion War Machine" and made a map trade routes and Dominion weak points. The meeting ended shortly before the battle, which meant that Ilsa and the other attendees were forced to run the Dominion blockade in order to leave the system.

Viper probe XJ9-CS14 was deployed from the Dominion II-class Dreadhull Stalker and eventually located the Insurgent base. On the ground, Commander Tavin Vossar spotted the probe droid crash while on a reconnaissance mission on his snowstrider —indigenous snow-lizards utilized by League personnel as mounts—and believing it to be a meteorite, went closer to investigate. On his way, Vossar was attacked by a native frostmaw and dragged off into a cave before he could get a closer look. Dace Rennick eventually went off to rescue Vossar during a harsh snowstorm, in spite of the concern from his comrades.

25.title: Battle of Kryvel
25.text: Later, Rennick and Grawlok were tasked with investigating the lead that Vossar came across, leading to their discovery of the existence of the probe droid. Upon being spotted by it, Dace attempted to destroy it, only to have droid activate its self-destruct mechanism. Receiving new intelligence from the probe, the crew of the Executor-class Star Dreadnought Executor initially dismissed the findings. In spite of Admiral Kendal Ostrel's concern that pictures of the Insurgent shield generator merely belonged to smugglers, Xarn Velgor instructed the Dominion Death Squadron to invade the planet. With their location revealed, the wrath of the Dominion would soon be unleashed upon the Insurgency. ## The battle

26.title: Battle of Kryvel
26.text:
### Plan Kay One Zero

Upon dissemination of Dace Rennick's report on the probe, base commander General Hallorin correctly concluded that the mysterious probe had been sent from the Dominion. Hallorin ordered the immediate evacuation of Frostpoint Base, using code K-one-zero. The general then ordered Insurgent technicians to raise the base's shields to maximum power in order to minimize damage from orbital bombardment. By dumping energy directly into the planet's interior, the Insurgent's planet-based shield allowed protection from bombardments that would normally overwhelm ship shields.

27.title: Battle of Kryvel
27.text: Simultaneously, Princess Ilsa Marrow instructed Insurgent pilots within Hangar 7 to escape in groups in order to avoid the Dominion blockade. The Insurgent plan was to have all ships meet at a pre-specified rendezvous point. Immediately, the rebel base fluttered with activity, and boarding began on thirty GR-75 medium transports, which had assembled at the base's north entrance. Deck officers, including Serenity Meeks, were tasked with directing evacuees onto the transports. Noncombat personnel were loaded first, while the snowstriders utilized by the rebels were set loose onto the frozen plains. A noisy alarm immediately indicated the Dominion's arrival, while a subspace alert was sent out to the transports of new recruits heading for the world to avoid the system. The journalist Corwi Selgrothe was one of the non-combatants in the base; when the Dominion arrived, she initially attempted to record Marrow's actions before bumping into the rebel soldier L'cayo Llem, who led her to a GR-75.

28.title: Battle of Ostara
28.text:
# Battle of Ostara

The Battle of Ostara, also known as the Battle of the Void Core or the Miracle of Ostara, was a major and decisive battle of the Sundering War, in which the Free League was able to destroy the Void Core and was seen as one of the first major victories over the Dominion of Astra.

29.title: Battle of Ostara
29.text:
## Prelude

During the Battle of Corall, Mira Halden and Dorin Sorrel managed to steal detailed plans and design specifications for the Dominion battle station known as the Void Core and transmit them to the League Fleet above; these plans soon made their way to Princess Ilsa Marrow. Princess Ilsa was able to place the Void Core plans within K7-T4. Shortly after Dominion forces under the command of the Dark Lord of the Morrak, Xarn Velgor, soon captured Princess Ilsa and the crew of the Valiant IV.

Princess Ilsa was taken prisoner aboard the Void Core by Lord Velgor to Grand Prefect Corvin Vessic. The Princess was rescued from captivity by an unlikely alliance of the smuggler Dace Rennick, former Aethari Master Odrin Halvane, a young farmboy from Drysa named Tavin Vossar, and Rennick's First Mate, the Varrsk named Grawlok. The group, which also included Free League droids K7-T4 and V-9LX, in possession of the Void Core plans, fled to the Insurgent base on Ostara IV —closely pursued by Vessic and the battle station.

Before Marrow arrived, Chancellor Ysa Talvorn was evacuated aboard a shuttle, as General Harlow considered her the core of the rebellion. During her time away, she composed a contingency plan: surrender to Sovereign Crayle.

30.title: Battle of Ostara
30.text:
Before Marrow arrived, Chancellor Ysa Talvorn was evacuated aboard a shuttle, as General Harlow considered her the core of the rebellion. During her time away, she composed a contingency plan: surrender to Sovereign Crayle.

General Jan Harlow briefed the rebel pilots on the plan. The Void Core's defenses were designed for a direct, large-scale assault. By using small, one-man starfighters, the Insurgents would slip through the Void Core's main defenses, maneuver down a narrow trench leading to the exhaust port, and fire proton torpedoes into the exhaust port. An analysis of the plans identified a weakness in the battle station, placed there by Dominion scientist Orrin Halden: a small thermal exhaust port leading to the main reactor. A proton torpedo fired into the port would cause a chain reaction that would destroy the battle station. ## The battle

31.title: Battle of Ostara
31.text:
### The approach

With the Void Core approaching, Bulwarks from Gold Squadron and Lancers from Red Squadron and Green Squadron were dispatched to carry out the attack plan. A total of 30 ships were deployed in the assault on the Void Core: 8 Bulwarks from Gold Squadron as well as 22 Lancers, 12 from Red Squadron and the other 10 from Green Squadron. The starfighters weaved through the turret emplacements, destroying many as they passed. Red Six (Jek Tono Barrow) was the first to be destroyed in the volley of turret fire. The deployment of Dominion Rak fighters, including one piloted by Lieutenant Iden Versio, devastated the Insurgent attackers, destroying them far faster and more efficiently than the station's weapon emplacements had been able to. Red Four (John D. Branon) was the first to be shot down by the incoming TIEs.

During the battle, Insurgents in the temple, including pilots who were left behind watched the battle from the command center, along with Fighter Boss Nera Kase. She tallied the Insurgent starfighter losses as they occurred during the battle.

32.title: Battle of Ostara
32.text: Some time into the battle, Dominion officer Jude Edivon aboard the Void Core identified the threat of the Insurgents' attack strategy, and attempted to warn her superiors of the danger. However, Grand Prefect Vessic ignored the warning and refused to evacuate. Informed by Lieutenant Tanbris that the Insurgents were avoiding the turbolaser fire, Velgor himself decided to deploy a squadron of Rak fighters to destroy the remaining Insurgent fighters. This would be the only Dominion squadron launched during the battle. Velgor himself would join the battle, entering the fray aboard his personal Rak Advanced as Black Leader. He was joined by two other members of Black Squadron, the Rak pilot aces "Backstabber" and Black Two Mithel, as his hand-picked wingmen.

33.title: Battle of Ostara
33.text:
### Trench run

The first attack run was performed by a trio of Bulwarks from Gold Squadron. The three Bulwarks, led by Gold Leader (Jon Vander) with Gold Two (Dex Tiree) and Gold Five (Davish Krail) escorting, attempted to make a shot on the exhaust port but were shot down by Velgor. A second trench run was performed by a trio of Lancers from Red Squadron flown by Red Leader (Garven Dreis), Red Ten (Theron Nett), and Red Twelve (Puck Naeco). Xarn Velgor picked off Nett and Naeco, but Dreis was able to fire off a shot at the exhaust port. However, his proton torpedoes missed their mark, only scratching the surface. Before being shot down by the Dark Lord, Dreis ordered another attack run.

Following the final command of Red Leader, Red Five (Tavin Vossar) led the final attempt with Red Two (Brann Marek) and Red Three, Tavin's old friend, (Tobin Darklighter), as wingmen. Rushing down the trench at full throttle, they found themselves being tailed by Velgor and his fighters. One of Velgor's wingmen damaged Marek' fighter, forcing him to disengage, whilst Velgor personally destroyed Darklighter's Lancer, forcing Vossar to attempt the shot on his own. In this dire moment the Insurgent leaders were concerned when the young pilot deactivated his targeting system for the attempt, but Vossar assured them that nothing was wrong; he was advised by the spirit of Halvane to rely on the Flux instead for his attack.

34.title: Battle of Ostara
34.text: For his part, Velgor sensed this power himself and found firing on the fighter unusually difficult, with his single hit only putting K7-T4, who was serving as the fighter's astromech droid, out of commission. When the Dark Lord prepared to finally shoot down the enemy, his wingman Backstabber was suddenly shot down from above beside him. The source of that attack was the Crimson Kestrel diving out of the nearby star's light. Dace Rennick and Grawlok, believed to have abandoned the Insurgents prior to the assault, unexpectedly returned to assist Vossar in his most desperate moment. Grawlok had been urging Rennick to return, with Rennick's conscience finally getting the better of him when he decided he needed to help Vossar, whom he had befriended.

35.title: Battle of Ostara
35.text:
### Destruction of the Void Core

Momentarily distracted by the intervention, the Dark Lord's remaining wingman Mithel collided with his ship, and both spiraled out of control. The Rak fighter pilot flew into the side of the trench and knocked Velgor away from the Void Core, and this allowed Vossar to fire his shot. With the aid of the Flux, the torpedoes shot along the trench and entered the shaft perfectly, as the two surviving Lancers, the lone surviving Bulwark and the aging freighter made for Ostara IV. The surviving rebel pilots included Vossar, Marek, and Gold Three (Evaan Verlaine).

36.title: Battle of Sylvar
36.text:
# Battle of Sylvar

The Battle of Sylvar, also known as the Mission to Sylvar, the assault on the second Void Core, or the attack on the second Void Core, was a major and decisive battle of the Sundering War, one in which the League to Restore the Concord shattered the rule of the Dominion of Astra and saw the destruction of the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and the deaths of Xarn Nocturne and Xarn Velgor. The triumph of the League over the Dominion, and the void left in the wake of the Sovereign's demise, gave the League the opportunity to give rise to the New Concord, which ultimately prevailed over the Dominion in the Battle of Saddar one year later. The legacy of the Battle of Sylvar reverberated for decades after the fighting ended, including into the brewing war between the Dominion-inspired Iron Mandate and the Ember Front that arose to combat it.

37.title: Battle of Sylvar
37.text: The origins of the Battle of Sylvar emerged from the discovery that the Dominion was using the Forest Moon of Sylvar as a staging ground to construct a second Void Core, the first of which had been destroyed four years earlier during the Battle of Ostara. Pelari spies employed by the League gained the intelligence needed to determine the Void Core's location and learn that the Sovereign planned to personally oversee the final phases of construction, though the League was unaware that this was an elaborate plot to destroy Tavin Vossar, a Aethari and the son of Xarn Velgor, and the League itself once and for all. The battle began after the League Fleet assembled near Sullust, and special operations ground forces were deployed to Sylvar to disable the shield protecting the armored battle station.

38.title: Battle of Sylvar
38.text: The League Fleet soon arrived to discover the Dominion Navy waiting for them, along with a fully operational Void Core. Allied with the native Nubbits, ground forces under the command of General Dace Rennick and Princess Ilsa Marrow destroyed the shield, allowing the League Fleet to attack the superweapon. Meanwhile, Vossar engaged Velgor in a final lumeblade duel aboard the Void Core. After defeating his father, the Sovereign betrayed Velgor by attempting to convince the Aethari Knight to kill Velgor and turn to the dark side of the Flux, only for Tavin to refuse. To save his son from the wrath of the Sovereign, Velgor surprised and betrayed Nocturne, killing the Dark Lord of the Morrak, and sacrificing his own life in the process—an act that fulfilled the Aethari prophecy of the Foretold One and brought balance to the Flux. Shortly thereafter, the Free League forces destroyed the Void Core. Dominion forces were left in tatters, enabling the League to form the New Concord and forge a new future free of the Morrak and the rule of the Dominion, thus allowing the Aethari Order to be restored. ## Prelude

39.title: Battle of Sylvar
39.text:
### Background

Unlike the Battle of Ostara, the last major battle between the League to Restore the Concord and the Dominion of Astra, which had taken place on the ice world of Kryvel, had resulted in a disastrous defeat for the League. The loss of the recently established Frostpoint Base forced the League High Command to break the League Fleet into small task forces that would constantly jump from one star system to another to prevent another defeat for Dominion propagandists to celebrate. Still, the Battle of Kryvel showed the rebellion would escape and survive, instead of stand and fight, if discovered. As such, the key to destroying the rebellion laid not with finding its gathering area but luring it to a choke point. However, the Battle of Ostara showed that, in order to trick the rebels into staying in one place to fight, the Dominion would need a great threat the rebels had no choice but to face.

During Scarlet Veil's ill-fated war against the Dominion, Dawn agents Bevelyn and Jon Melton revealed the existence of the second Void Core to the Free League. The Pelari Spynet, in time, intercepted information that revealed the Dominion was building the station in orbit over the forest moon of Sylvar. The Dominion had occupied the moon for the Void Core project, thereby bringing Dominion forces into conflict with the native Nubbits. With the Dominion largely paying the Nubbits no mind, only seeing them as annoyances instead of a threat, they failed to recognize the dangers the native lifeforms could cause and did not notice the species had a strong warrior culture.

40.title: Battle of Sylvar
40.text: Thanks to the Pelari spies, the League also learned that Galactic Sovereign Aldus Crayle, otherwise known as the Dark Lord of the Morrak Xarn Nocturne, was to oversee the completion of the Void Core II, the construction of which was otherwise being overseen by Prefect Tiaan Velkor. Unbeknownst to the League, the Sovereign had allowed the location of the second Void Core to be leaked and established a trap, foreseeing the League's plan. The Dominion had leaked the location of the new Void Core with the hope the totemic symbolism the battle station held would draw out the rebellion for a major battle, in which the Free League Navy could be crushed in a surprise trap. Beyond that, the Dominion ensured that the rebels learned that Crayle himself would be present, thereby making the Void Core an even more important target for the rebels.

41.title: Battle of Sylvar
41.text:
### Baiting the trap

To bait the trap, Dominion Intelligence leaked the information that fell into the hands of the Pelari spies, ensuring the League obtained incomplete information about the Void Core: the League learned that Crayle would be present but was tricked into thinking that the battle station's superlaser was inoperative, when in fact the battle station would be fully operational. In addition to maintaining a skilled legion on Sylvar's surface to counter a rebel ground assault, which the League would need to launch to disable the Void Core shield generator on Sylvar's surface, the Sovereign would also hide a large fleet of Dreadhulls on the far side of Sylvar so as to entrap the fleet. However, Prefect Derrek Raythe had sent a message containing orders for Death Squadron to join the fleet at Sylvar. To keep the information secretive, commander Iden Versio from the special forces Inferno Squad, was sent to the Invincible Faith and deleted it.

42.title: Battle of Sylvar
42.text: Ultimately, the Dominion prepared itself to face the rebellion on a spacefront and battlefront under its complete control, with the looming threat of the Nubbits not something the regime realized would be a danger —unbeknownst to the Dominion personnel, the Nubbits actively prepared to attack the bunker and, over the course of several weeks, established defensive positions around the facility which would prove vital in the battle to come. So as to capture the inevitable rebel ground team, Crayle selected Tempest Flux, an elite formation composed of some of his finest troops, to be garrisoned on Sylvar, where Tempest Flux reinforced the shield generator personnel. As the deployment continued, whole squads were lost to the dark forests of Sylvar.

43.title: Crimson Kestrel
43.text:
# Crimson Kestrel

The Crimson Kestrel, originally designated YT 492727ZED and formerly known as the Stellar Envoy, and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell, Corell's Pride, Close Shave, Fickle Flyer, Foul Matter, Graphite Skipper, Jin-Den Smoke, Longshot, Lost and Found, Star Princess, Sunfighter Franchise, Sweet Suprise, Meetyl's Misery, Wayward Son, and Victory Ring, was a Dravosi KR-900 light freighter built around 60 BVC. Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Dace Rennick and Grawlok before, during, and following the Sundering War.

44.title: Crimson Kestrel
44.text: During the Kestrel ' s time in the possession of the smuggler Teodor Vashell, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Dace Rennick's famous record-breaking Varn Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Rennick won it from Vashell shortly afterwards in a game of tarrok. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a slipdrive engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominion Dreadhulls. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Ilsa Marrow in 1 BVC to evade Dominion legionnaires. Afterwards, the Crimson Kestrel saw further action when Rennick chose to join the Free League during the Battle of Ostara, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Xarn Velgor's Rak Advanced, allowing Tavin Vossar to fire the proton torpedoes from his T-65B Lancer starfighter that destroyed the Void Core.

45.title: Crimson Kestrel
45.text:
After Rennick was captured on Nimbara, Vashell took command of the Kestrel once more to search for him. In 4 AVC, following Rennick's rescue, Vashell flew the ship at the Battle of Sylvar, where it entered the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Rennick's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Plutt on Saddar, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Kestrel was eventually stolen by the Flux-sensitive scavenger Nira, former Iron Mandate legionnaire Jorel, and Ember Front droid QT-3 to escape the forces of the Iron Mandate in 34 AVC. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Rennick and Grawlok.

Following Rennick's death soon after, the Crimson Kestrel became a Ember Front vessel piloted by its new owner, Nira, throughout much of the Iron Mandate-Ember Front War. In 35 AVC, the ship was once again captained by Vashell during the Battle of Umbrath, which saw a decisive victory for the Ember Front and Aethari Order, before being returned to Nira, who had been newly dubbed a Vossar.

46.title: Crimson Kestrel
46.text:
## Description

The Crimson Kestrel was a KR-900 light freighter of the YT-1300f variety. Its basic shape was defined by two convex saucers welded together, a pair of front-facing mandibles and an outrigger-style, side-mounted cockpit with transparisteel viewports. Apart from the shape of its chassis, the Kestrel retained very little of its off-the-dock instrumentation. Because its successive owners either upgraded or downgraded every system according to their personal specifications, the freighter ended up becoming a unique ship. These customizations, however, came at the price of reliability, and the Kestrel was known to suffer frequent breakdowns in the heat of battle. After the circular military-grade sensor dish was lost during the Battle of Sylvar, the dish was replaced with the base rectangular model which was originally supplied with the ship. During the Battle of Saltmere, the Kestrel again lost its rectenna, and it was replaced with a military-grade rectenna similar to that of the one lost during the Battle of Sylvar. Additionally, the Kestrel had a dejarik table, which was installed by Teodor Vashell when upgrading the ship, featuring creatures found throughout the galaxy for the amusement of passengers and crew.

47.title: Crimson Kestrel
47.text:
### Engines

The Crimson Kestrel ' s Girodyne SRB42 sublight engines were heavily modified through the addition of a SLAM overdrive that rerouted energy for acceleration bursts. As a result, the ship could fly at a maximum speed of 1,200 kilometer per hour in atmosphere and 3,000 G in space. The stock slipdrive of the KR-900 series was replaced with a Isu-Sim SSP05. Although the regular SSP05 was a Class 1 slipdrive, the one that equipped the Kestrel had been jury-rigged " Vandangante style " into a Class 0.5 drive —twice as fast as most warships of the Dominion of Astra. According to Ralsius Paldora, the Crimson Kestrel ' s slipdrive failed 1.22 times more than the one on the YT-2400 light freighter. In addition to its renowned slipdrive, which supposedly made the Kestrel the "fastest ship in the galaxy," the ship was equipped with a backup slipdrive. It was much slower than the primary engine and often took several weeks or months to reach the nearest star system. A component of the engines was the engine coupling which caused the Kestrel to malfunction when misaligned.

48.title: Crimson Kestrel
48.text:
### Armament, hull, and shields

The weaponry of the Crimson Kestrel was normally suited for a much larger warship. It included two CEC AG-2G quad laser cannons (one ventral and one dorsal) with enhanced laser actuators and gas feeds, which gave them maximum range and damage. These served as its primary defensive armament, able to destroy enemy fighters with a single direct hit. Between the forward mandibles, there were two Arakyd ST2 concussion missile tubes, each of which carried a four- missile magazine. Additionally, a BlasTech Ax-108 "Ground Buzzer" blaster cannon mounted near the ventral boarding ramp allowed its crew to defend the ship against infantry and other light targets while on the ground. Duralloy plates salvaged from an Dominion cruiser afforded the Kestrel capital ship-class hull armor. The ship was also equipped with ion cannons, which could be activated instead of its typical laser cannons.

The ship had three deflector shield generators: the bow was protected from both lasers and concussion missiles by Torplex and Nordoxicon units, while a Kuat Drive Yards generator shielded the stern. This, combined with its heavy armor, made the Kestrel tough enough to even withstand direct hits from turbolaser fire of star destroyers.

49.title: Crimson Kestrel
49.text: The Kestrel ' s combination of sublight speed and maneuverability was comparable to most of the starfighters fielded by the Insurgency and Dominion, while its shielding, slipdrive, heavy armor and weapons were on par with those typically found on capital ships. These traits made it an ideal choice for General Teodor Vashell's attack run within the bowels of the Void Core during the Battle of Sylvar. While agile and almost near impervious to almost all heavy weapons and turbolasers as any large warship, the Kestrel ' s only real combat weakness was its sheer size in comparison to starfighters. Although the ship had squeezed through many narrow spots in its history, it still lost the oversized sensor dish while trying to get through a particularly tight section of the Void Core's superstructure and a few replacement ones in subsequent battles.

50.title: Dace Rennick
50.text:
# Dace Rennick

Dace Rennick, known only as Dace until being given the surname Rennick, was a human male smuggler and hero of the League to Restore the Concord. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Crimson Kestrel, a leader in the Free League and an instrumental figure in the Sundering War during the reign of the Dominion of Astra. Although he did not believe in the Flux controlling his destiny, Dace came to believe in the cause of galactic freedom, joining Aethari Tavin Vossar and Princess Ilsa Marrow in the fight for the Insurgency. Following the war, Dace and Ilsa welcomed a son, Corin Rennick, who became the dark knight Vael Durn after being corrupted by the dark side of the Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Ilsa hoped that Dace, as Corin's father, could find a way to break the dark side's hold on their son. Dace Rennick became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Insurgency.

51.title: Dace Rennick
51.text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Dravos, Dace yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow scrumrat named Sava, Dace lived as a street thief with Dravos's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Proxima went bad, causing Dace to flee Dravos. He was given the full name "Dace Rennick" by an Dominion recruitment officer while entering the Dominion Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Dominion cadet, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominion Armored Division. On Mimban, Dace met the thief Tobias Hollis and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined coaxium from Varn in order to pay a debt to Dryden Vos, a kingpin with the Scarlet Veil crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Sava, Dace was forced to kill his mentor Hollis after a brutal double-cross. Dace also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Teodor Vashell and the Varrsk Grawlok, the latter who became his best friend. Vashell owned the Crimson Kestrel, a fast ship with which Dace made the Varn Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Teodor in a game of tarrok.

52.title: Dace Rennick
52.text: With only Grawlok remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Dravosi smuggler, Dace Rennick embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Hrask the Vogg, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Drysa. After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Rennick owed a great deal of money to Hrask, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Dace and Grawlok were hired to charter Tavin Vossar, Odrin Halvane, and the droids K7-T4 and V-9LX to Seravel, avoiding Dominion legionnaires who were searching for Tavin's droids. However, as they find Seravel destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Rennick became caught up in the rebellion against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Ilsa Marrow, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Insurgent base on Ostara IV, and saved Tavin from the Morrak Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Ostara, allowing Vossar to destroy the Void Core. Rennick fought with the Insurgency for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.

53.title: Dace Rennick
53.text:
After the Battle of Kryvel, Rennick sought refuge with Marrow—with whom he had fallen in love—Grawlok, and V-9LX on Sky Haven, which was operated by his old friend Teodor Vashell. There, they were captured by Xarn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Vossar to the city. Rennick was frozen in stasium and taken to Hrask's Palace on Drysa by the bounty hunter Jask Morvain, where he remained encased in stasium for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the League Fleet, Rennick was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Sylvar. Rennick led the Pathfinders to Sylvar, where he, Marrow, Grawlok, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Nubbits, destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the League Fleet to destroy the superweapon.

The Battle of Sylvar, which saw the deaths of Sovereign Aldus Crayle and Xarn Velgor, allowed the Insurgency to form the New Concord. In the early days after Sylvar, Rennick continued to lead the Pathfinders against the Dominion. He married Marrow, and the two had a son, Corin Rennick. The boy struggled with the dark side of the Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Xarn Velgor and twin sister of Tavin Vossar, Corin was Flux-sensitive —so Marrow sent him to be trained as a Aethari by Vossar. Corin was seduced to the dark side by Gorrath, Supreme Leader of the Iron Mandate, resulting in the destruction of Vossar's attempt to rebuild the Aethari Order.

54.title: Dace Rennick
54.text: Having lost their son, Rennick left and returned to smuggling, and even lost the Crimson Kestrel to numerous thieves. He continued to smuggle until he was brought back into the fight by a scavenger named Nira and a defected Iron Mandate legionnaire named Jorel, who carried with them a droid, QT-3, that had part of a map to Vossar's location. Rennick, who retrieved the Kestrel from Nira and Jorel, returned to Marrow, who led the Ember Front against the Iron Mandate, and fought in the battle to destroy the Iron Mandate superweapon known as Sunreaver Base. During the battle, Rennick saw his son, who had taken the name Vael Durn, and tried to convince him to return home. Instead, Durn stabbed his father with his lumeblade. Mortally wounded, Rennick fell to his death in the bowels of the Sunreaver weapon. However, Rennick's heroic memory survived and his spirit remained alive and appeared in a Flux vision a year later to convince Durn to abandon the dark side and defeat the resurrected Xarn Nocturne, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Nira and Durn, being enough for Corin Rennick to return and eventually sacrifice his own life to help Nira end Nocturne and the Morrak for good.

55.title: Dace Rennick
55.text:
## Biography

### Early life

Dace was born in a rough-and-tumble favela on the planet Dravos during the waning years of the Concord of Worlds in 32 BVC. Sometime after he became famous, it would be rumored by a Snivvian bounty hunter that Dace was actually a descendant of the Prince-Admiral Jonashe Rennick, a member of the ancient Dravosi royalty. During his formative years, his father Ovan worked in the Dravosi Engineering Corporation shipyards, building vessels such as KR-900 light freighters until he was laid off. Rennick's father wished he could leave Dravos on such a ship, but was never able to afford to. According to Dace, he was never close with his father. At one point his father brought him to the freighter factory where he worked and pointed out to the young Dace that the ships being built there were his contributions to the galaxy, but that they ultimately didn't matter. He advised him that he wasn't meant to build ships, but rather to fly the ships. Eventually, his father abandoned him. At some point he met the Ithorian Pjolan.

56.title: Dominion of Astra
56.text:
# Dominion of Astra

The Dominion of Astra, also known as the First Dominion of Astra, the Dominion regime, Crayle's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a totalitarian stratocratic fascist dictatorship that replaced the Concord of Worlds at the end of the Mirror Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the League to Restore the Concord in the Sundering War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.

57.title: Dominion of Astra
57.text: The Dominion traced its origins to a Morrak conspiracy to destroy the Aethari Order and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Morrak, for the Galactic Sovereign was, in fact, the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Xarn Velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Aethari and anti-droid sentiment and human - ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Mirror Wars, Xarn Nocturne appointed himself Sovereign at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Concord. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Galactic Assembly, Xarn Nocturne staged a coup by the Aethari and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Xarn Velgor.

58.title: Dominion of Astra
58.text: The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Assembly and the spreading of its massive technological military force across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Dominion of Astra was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Assembly waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing rebellion, winning its first major victory over Pyrrhos in 4 BVC. These rebel groups eventually formed the Free League in 2 BVC, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Corall, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Ostara. The following years saw initial League successes until a major Dominion victory on Kryvel in 3 AVC, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Sylvar. During the battle, Xarn Nocturne was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Kaelen Vossar, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Morrak rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Concord of Worlds, the New Concord.

59.title: Dominion of Astra
59.text:
With the deaths of the Sovereign and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Prefects, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Tor Ostrak's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Concord. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rae Merrin, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Vorn. Ultimately, Vorn seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Merrin from power and becoming Sovereign-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Vorn's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Saddar in 5 AVC, ultimately losing and capitulating to the New Concord. With the cessation of the fighting, the Galactic Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.

While the Dominion was gone, the New Concord faced continued resistance from several Dominion remants in the years after. Eventually its successor, the Iron Mandate began a clandestine armament program to rebuild the former Dominion Military. The miltary junta was unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Umbrath attended to the spirit of Xarn Nocturne, and constructed a fleet built to turn the Iron Mandate into a true empire. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Ember Front and Aethari Order, leading to an end of the Iron Mandate. ## History

60.title: Dominion of Astra
60.text:
### Early foundations

The Dominion ideals of the Dominion of Astra could be dated back to the Morrak Dominion of the Old Concord's time period. Following the defeat of the Morrak during their final war with the Aethari Order, for at least a thousand years, the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Concord of Worlds, which was governed by the Galactic Assembly and led by an elected Supreme Chancellor.

In the last decades of its existence, the Concord Assembly became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Xarn Nocturne, the Dark Lord of the Morrak known publicly as Delegate Aldus Crayle of Lirael, privately lamented the declining state of the Assembly, noting that the Concord was "not what it once was."

Thirteen years before the Concord's end as a democracy, Xarn Nocturne orchestrated the Invasion of Lirael by the Mercantile Combine in order to create a leadership crisis in the Assembly. Nocturne used the crisis to manipulate the then Queen of the Lirael, Selene Corvane, into calling a Vote of No Confidence against sitting Supreme Chancellor Aurel Esteven. The vote passed, and in the subsequent election, Nocturne—in his public persona of Delegate Crayle of Lirael —secured the position of Supreme Chancellor of the Concord of Worlds for himself through a strong sympathy vote. Ultimately, he would be the last individual to hold this office.

61.title: Dominion of Astra
61.text: In the decade that followed, Nocturne secretly manipulated galactic events to the extent that war became inevitable. Besides persuading a dead Aethari Master, Talo-Venn, to create a secret replicant army, he also tasked his Morrak apprentice, Xarn Vexus, with exacerbating political tensions in the Concord and engineering a Secessionist Crisis. These actions would culminate in the outbreak of the Mirror Wars held on Karrik, the last conflict of the Concord, while Nocturne himself "reluctantly" accepted emergency powers from the Assembly. The Mirror Wars, Nocturne planned, would further make people in the galaxy grow bitter with the Concord while he centralized his power to sweep away the Concord and Aethari.

62.title: Dominion of Astra
62.text:
### Birth of the New Order

Since the onset of the Mirror Wars in 22 BVC, the Concord endeavored to strengthen its security and stability through the creation of new organizations such as the Commission for the Protection of the Concord (COMPOR), which utilized propaganda to increase public morale, promote patriotism, and foster anti-Secessionist sentiment within the general population. As the Concord became increasingly centralized, however, Chancellor Crayle's powers continued to grow through additional assets ceded to the Office of the Chancellor, including the galactic banking system that was placed under his direct oversight. This gave Nocturne the finance he needed to build his empire. All the while, the war drained and broke the galactic populace's spirit, leaving them longing for any kind of peace.

63.title: Drysa
63.text:
# Drysa

Drysa was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Far Reach Territories. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Skerrit and Dunewalker Raider species and of Kaelen and Tavin Vossar, who would go on to shape galactic history.

It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers, which were later used by the Skerrit population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Vogg Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

64.title: Drysa
64.text:
Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Drysa gained the notice of the Dominion of Astra during the Sundering War when an escape pod carrying two droids in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Far Reach world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Hrask Garrak Tiure of the Vogg Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Free League cell on Drysa that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.

Following the death of Hrask and the withdrawal of Dominion forces after the Battle of Sylvar, an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Jask Morvain returned and took over Hrask's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Vogg Clan and the Krell Syndicate, the new Daimyo was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Drysa. With help from the Vardian Kai Torvane, Morvain rallied the denizens of the settlements Dune Reach and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

65.title: Drysa
65.text:
## Description

Drysa was a hot desert planet located in the Far Reach, a region of the galaxy far removed from its core. It had three moons, Ghomrassen, Guermessa, and Chenini. Drysa orbited twin suns, Tatoo I and Tatoo II. According to Skerrit folklore, the desert known as the Dune Sea was once a true ocean. The whole planet was covered in harsh deserts, and only a small part of its northern hemisphere could sustain intelligent life. The landscape was covered with sand dunes, mountains, and canyons, which made traversing the planet very difficult. Due to the absence of surface water, those who lived on Drysa had to draw moisture through the dry air.

Rain was incredibly rare on Drysa, coming once a year, decade, or century. When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species, the largest of which were the carnivorous krayt dragons. The common krayt dragon, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater krayt dragon, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common grazer and eopie species also found a home on the world, along with dewbacks, rontos, womp rats, massiffs, and scurriers.

66.title: Drysa
66.text: The cities of Drysa were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living. ## History

67.title: Drysa
67.text:
### Early history

Drysa was the homeworld of the Skerrit and Dunewalker Raider species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Lehon, Drysa had also been inhabited by a group called the Kumumgah during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Drysa's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

As a result of sporadic and unsuccessful colonization ventures, the planet became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants attempted to earn a living in the wastes. A long-ago mining boom saw the widespread use of sandcrawlers on the desert plains in an effort to mine valuable minerals. However, after it was discovered that most valuable minerals could be found on the surface, along with most minerals having unwanted metallurgic properties, the sandcrawlers were abandoned and eventually picked up by the native Skerrits for use as shelter and mobile bases, from which they collected scrap from thousands of years of crashed spacecraft and failed mining projects.

68.title: Drysa
68.text:
Offworlders erected various cities in the desert, and colonists who decided to stay on the planet built moisture farms. The B'omarr Order on Drysa kept their disembodied brains floating in jars that hung below their spider-like droid bodies, and built a monastery on the planet which would eventually come under the ownership of Hrask Garrak Tiure as his palace.

Most wealth eventually found its way into the city of Dune Reach, with most of it procured from gambling and off-world trade, especially through the lucrative black market. The influx of commercial ventures fueled Dune Reach's growth, eventually securing its regional importance as a hub of economic and financial activity. With high tariffs imposed by the Voggs, some believed themselves able to escape paying them by doing business in the planet's de facto capital, however often found themselves scammed and broke if not through gambling, through simple bad luck.

69.title: Drysa
69.text:
### Scum and villainy

In the last decades of the Concord of Worlds, Drysa was known as a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, including slavery. The sand people regularly attacked Fort Dunewalker, earning them their name of "Dunewalker Raiders." It was home to a human slave named Maela Vossar and her son Kaelen.

During this period, Queen Selene Corvane of Lirael escaped the capture of her homeworld by the Mercantile Combine, and she took refuge on Drysa with her companions and protectors, including the Aethari Master Ardel Strosk and his apprentice Odrin Halvane. The Vossars befriended Corvane's party, and the young slave ended up participating in a skyrun to help his new friends obtain a new T-14 slipdrive generator for their damaged starship. After discovering that Kaelen Vossar would make an exceptional recruit for the Aethari Order, Master Ardel Strosk managed to obtain his freedom from the junk dealer Grubbo in the city of Dune Reach, and the Queen's party left Drysa with the boy. After participating in numerous adventures, including the Invasion of Lirael, the former Drysan slave joined the Aethari Order under Halvane's tutelage.

70.title: Grawlok
70.text:
# Grawlok

Grawlok, known affectionately to his friends as Grawie, was a Varrsk male warrior, smuggler, mechanic, pilot, and resistance fighter who fought in the Mirror Wars, the Sundering War, the Cold War, and the subsequent Iron Mandate-Ember Front War. He hailed from the planet Grovath where he was born during the High Concord Era and became a Varrsk military leader. During the Mirror Wars, he was captured by Saurak slavers and held captive on Wasskah, but he worked with a fellow captive, Aethari Commander Lirra Sef, to escape. He later commanded Varrsk forces of the Rowantree Varrsk Militia during the Battle of Grovath alongside the Grand Army of the Concord, led by Aethari General Morro. During the battle, one of the last ones of the war, Morro's replicant troopers received Directive Nine from the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne and, with the help of Grawlok and his fellow Varrsk Chieftain and General Rakkor, Morro escaped Grovath and the destruction of the Aethari Order.

71.title: Grawlok
71.text: In the years that followed, during the rule of the Dominion of Astra, Grawlok was enslaved by the Dominion until he was rescued by Corporal Dace Rennick, becoming his co-pilot aboard the Crimson Kestrel during a raid on Varn for Scarlet Veil with Tobias Hollis and Sava. Winning the Kestrel from Teodoric Amsel Vashell, they later worked in the employ of crime lord Hrask the Vogg until Rennick was forced to dump a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Dominion, at which point a bounty was placed on their heads. Soon thereafter, Grawlok and Rennick were hired by Aethari Master Odrin Halvane to ferry him, Tavin Vossar, V-9LX, and K7-T4 to Seravel on a mission vital to the survival of the League to Restore the Concord. After finding Seravel was destroyed, the group was brought aboard the Void Core, where they helped Princess Ilsa Marrow escape from captivity and return to the Insurgent base on Ostara IV. Though Grawlok and Rennick initially chose to leave Ostara IV and not join the Insurgency, they ended up fighting in the Battle of Ostara and were instrumental in Vossar's destruction of the Void Core, a major victory for the Insurgency.

72.title: Grawlok
72.text: Throughout the war, Grawlok and Rennick fought the Dominion in a number of engagements, including an assault on Cymoon 1 and the battle on Vrogas Vas. Along with Princess Marrow and V-9LX, they escaped from Frostpoint Base on the planet Kryvel after the Dominion tracked the Free League there. The group sought refuge with Vashell on Sky Haven, but Vashell betrayed them and turned them over to Xarn Velgor, the Sovereign's chief enforcer, after his city was threatened. Rennick was frozen in stasium and Vashell helped the others escape, but they were too late to save the frozen Rennick from being taken by Jask Morvain to Hrask the Vogg. Grawlok and Vashell set off to find Rennick and located him in Hrask's Palace on Drysa, where Grawlok and his friends saved Rennick and destroyed Hrask. Shortly thereafter, they fought in the Battle of Sylvar, where Grawlok helped destroy the shield generator and allowed the League Fleet to destroy the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station. Nocturne was killed for the first time aboard the battle station, delivering a crippling blow to the Dominion.

73.title: Grawlok
73.text: After Sylvar and the rise of the New Concord, Grawlok and Rennick fought to liberate Grovath from the Dominion. When the war finally came to a close, Grawlok returned home to Grovath with his family. After Rennick's son Corin, turned to the dark side and destroyed Vossar's new generation of Aethari, Grawlok reunited with his old friend and the two spent many years as smugglers once more. They lost the Crimson Kestrel and ended up smuggling aboard a ship called the Eravana, but they eventually found the Kestrel and, with it, stowaways named Nira, Jorel, and the droid QT-3. The droid had part of a map that led to the exiled Tavin Vossar, so the group brought the map to the Ember Front that opposed the Iron Mandate, which had risen from the ashes of the Dominion of Astra. Grawlok soon fought in the assault to destroy Sunreaver Base, a devastating Iron Mandate superweapon, a conflict in which Rennick lost his life at the hands of his son. After the base was destroyed, Grawlok joined Nira in traveling to the planet Teyra on the Kestrel, where they found Tavin Vossar. After Rennick's death, Grawlok often served as the sole pilot of the Kestrel, including piloting the ship to aid the Ember Front during the Battle of Saltmere.

74.title: Grawlok
74.text:
Roughly a year after the battle of Saltmere, Grawlok was one of the last of the Ember Front. Having learned of the mysterious return of Xarn Nocturne, Grawlok and the crew of the Kestrel, now including Cass Orlen, traveled to the planets Dustfall and Kijimi to find a clue to how to find where the Sovereign was hiding, being reunited with his friend Vashell in the process.
