The quest nearly ended in Grawlok's apparent death, as Nira, having been revealed to be the Sovereign's granddaughter through his son, lashed out with dark power during a fight with Vael Durn and destroyed a Iron Mandate transport that she had thought Grawlok had been loaded onto, seemingly killing him.

However, Grawlok survived and was rescued by the Ember Front as they continued the quest. Nira eventually found Umbrath during a failed self-exile attempt to protect the galaxy from her becoming a Morrak, and led the charge during the battle that ensued later on. Nira finally killed her malevolent grandfather with the help of the returned Corin Rennick in the climax of the battle, while the Ember Front, joined by the Citizens' Fleet, progressively overpowered the Morrak Eternal's fleet, the Last Mandate, that Nocturne planned to unleash.

Having ultimately destroyed the Morrak once and for all, the Ember Front reveled in their victory, but also mourned their losses, including Ilsa, who had died of natural causes shortly after reaching out to her son and helping him turn back towards the light.

75.title: Grawlok
75.text:
## Biography

### Early life

A Varrsk male, Grawlok, nicknamed "Grawie," hailed from Grovath, a peaceful planet where he was born in the city of Rwookrrorro, one hundred and eighty years before the Mirror Wars to Attichitcuk and a female Varrsk. during the High Concord Era. He was married to a female named Mallatobuck, and had a family to support, including a son named Lumpawaroo. During his life, he explored Grovath, including the wildest reaches of its forests, from one pole to the other. His exploration hardened his footpads.

### The Mirror Wars

At some point during the Mirror Wars, a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Concord of Worlds and the Secessionists, Grawlok famously shielded his allies. Fighting with courage to defend both Grovath and the Concord, he served as a combat engineer while other Varrsk soldiers led the charge in battle. In 20 BVC, he was captured by a Saurak hunting guild led by Garnac; taken to Island Four on Wasskah to be their prey, his transport was attacked by a trio of Aethari apprentices—the Novitiate Lirra Sef and the fledglings Jinx and O-Mer, also prey of the Sauraks.

76.title: Grovath
76.text:
# Grovath

Grovath, also known as Planet Varrsk C to some humans in the Heart Worlds, was a wroshyr tree-covered forest planet located in the southwestern quadrant of the galaxy and the homeworld of the Varrsk species. Four millennia before the Battle of Ostara, Grovath was discovered by the Varrum Corporation, who enslaved the Varrsk population and renamed the planet G5-623, later to Edean. Using superior technology, the company managed to enslave the Varrsks until an uprising drove the oppressors away. During the Mirror Wars, Grovath was a member of the Concord of Worlds, and endured enslavement under the Dominion of Astra, the Concord's successor. Later, during the rise of the New Concord, Grovath was liberated with the help of Concord forces led by Dace Rennick.

77.title: Grovath
77.text:
## Description

Grovath was a temperate jungle planet orbiting around a single star located in the Mytaranor sector of the Middle Reach. The planet had a complement of three moons, one of which was orange. The planet had no axial tilt and a perfectly circular orbit, causing it to lack seasons. The center of the planet was covered with a tropical ocean belt, which contained a number of islands and large coral reefs.

Covered in wroshyr trees, Grovath served as homeworld to the Varrsk species. Native fauna, such as Can-cells would influence the design of starships by the Varrsk inhabitants, while great cities, such as Rowantree would be built into the planet's trees. The Kashyyykian wilds could be dangerous to many, thanks to dangerous animals, such as Terentateks or wyyyschokk spiders in addition to carnivorous plants, such as the jaw plant and saava.

The crash site of the prison ship Ashmead's Lock was known as the Black Forest. Varrsks believed that the Black Forest was cursed and haunted by bad spirits. By 5 AVC, sections of Grovath's forests had been deforested and several rivers had been drained. The Dominion also established undersea mining platforms. Mount Arayakyak was once a rainforest orchard known as the Cultivating Talon, which provided Varrsks with fruits, such as shi-shok. By the Dominion Era, it had been defoliated by a poisonous black mold.

Two years after the planet's liberation by the New Concord, much of the Black Forest had grown back. The growing forest was still littered with the remnants of Dominion machinery, including an AT-ACT walker.

78.title: Grovath
78.text:
Two years after the planet's liberation by the New Concord, much of the Black Forest had grown back. The growing forest was still littered with the remnants of Dominion machinery, including an AT-ACT walker.

Grovath was in the same star system as Trandosha, the home of the Saurak species, who were traditional enemies of the Varrsks.

79.title: Grovath
79.text:
## History

### The Zeffo and Varrum occupation

In its early history, the Zeffo, an ancient technologically advanced species, travelled to Grovath where they had contact with the Varrsks. Millennia before the Sundering War, the Predori prison ship Ashmead's Lock crashed on the planet when a nearby gravity well collapsed on itself.

Four millennia before the Battle of Ostara, Grovath was discovered by the Varrum Corporation, who renamed the planet G5-623, and later to Edean. Using superior technology, the company managed to enslave the Varrsks until an uprising drove the invaders away. That painful episode left lasting scars in the Varrsks' hearts.

### Concord Era

By 232 BVC, the Aethari Order had established a Aethari outpost on Grovath.

At some point prior to the Invasion of Lirael, Aethari Master Morro faced a terentatek on Grovath, accompanied by his then Novitiate Varkon. At another point, Aethari Master Eno Cordova was researching Zeffonian culture on Grovath, and befriended Varrsk chieftain Rakkor.

For twenty years, Grovath's Varrsks, as well as the Varrsk population of its colony planets, needed to repeatedly repel the Mercantile Combine.

80.title: Grovath
80.text:
### Mirror Wars

In the years following the Invasion of Lirael, the rogue Aethari Count Varkon fomented political turmoil on the planet. Due to its status as a major navigational point, Grovath was of prime strategic importance to the Concord of Worlds. After the Varrsks fought off its raiders, the Coalition of Free Systems attacked the planet toward the end of the Mirror Wars. During the battle for their homeworld, hundreds of the Varrsk's catamarans were deployed. Eventually, the Confederacy's invasion fleet was driven off by Aethari General Master Morro's taskforce, but a massive force of LM-432 crab droids, droid tanks, and gunships remained and occupied the Wawaatt Archipelago.

In the last days of the Mirror Wars, with the help of Morro and Aethari Master Lissara Unvel, the Grand Army of the Concord managed to get the upper hand over the Secessionists. However, shortly after that victory, the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord Aldus Crayle unilaterally transformed the government into the First Dominion of Astra. While Morro was able to escape from the replicant troopers that attacked him after the initiation of Directive Nine, Unvel was captured and taken to Stygeon Prime's prison, the Spire.

81.title: Grovath
81.text:
### Dominion repression

Despite Grovath's loyalty to the Concord, the self-appointed Sovereign had the Varrsks enslaved, and their planet itself was blockaded, when the Dominion launched a siege of the planet. Used as slave labor, the Dominion would utilize the Varrsks to cut down the planet's native wroshyr trees for lumber and farm food to feed the Dominion Army as well as send them off to labor camps and construction jobs, such as building the first Void Core, or for science and bio-weapon experiments. In addition to being occupied and enslaved, Grovath was also stripped of its name and designated Dominion territory G5-623.

Several months into Grovath's occupation, Saurak mercenaries were contracted by the Dominion and supplied with Incinerator tanks. Under the supervision of replicant legionnaires, the Sauraks were tasked with burning down large sectors of forest on the planet in an effort to make way for Dominion industrialization. Directive Nine survivor Novitiate Gungi later assisted a tribe of Varrsks in destroying a convoy of these tanks.

By 18 BVC, news of the Dominion subjugation of Grovath had spread to the news bulletins, leading the former Aethari Novitiate Lirra Sef to worry about her Varrsk friend Grawlok, who she had briefly met during the Mirror Wars.

82.title: Grovath
82.text:
By 18 BVC, news of the Dominion subjugation of Grovath had spread to the news bulletins, leading the former Aethari Novitiate Lirra Sef to worry about her Varrsk friend Grawlok, who she had briefly met during the Mirror Wars.

In 14 BVC, a rebel cell led by Garrick Dravin was present on Grovath and in conflict with the Dominion. During this fight, Directive Nine survivor Rhen Tavis and the crew of the Stinger Mantis arrived to continue their search for a Aethari memory prism. Dravin's cell assisted them in their search for Rakkor, whose resistance was using the Shadowlands as a sanctuary, but the majority of their forces were forced to retreat after being overwhelmed by the Dominion.

Rhen again traveled to Grovath when he received a communication that Rakkor was willing to meet. Back on Grovath, Rakkor instructed Rhen to seek answers at the top of the Origin Tree. On the way up, he was attacked by the Ninth Sister, whose ship was taken down by a large winged creature. Rhen found the creature wounded from the attack and healed it, granting him access to the top of the Origin tree via a flight on its back. Rhen is attacked once again by the Ninth Sister and defeated her.

83.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
83.text:
# Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick

Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick was a Flux-sensitive human Seravelian female politician, Aethari, and military leader who served in the League to Restore the Concord during the Dominion Era and the New Concord and Ember Front in the subsequent New Concord Era. Shortly after birth on Polis Massa, she was adopted into the House of Marrow —the Seravelian royal family—and was raised as Princess Ilsa Marrow of Seravel, a planet in the Heart Worlds known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Delegate Corran Aldren Marrow and his wife, Queen Ysolde Marrow, making her the heir to the Seravelian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Marrow devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Dominion of Astra and the Iron Mandate.

84.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
84.text: Born in 19 BVC as Ilsa Corvane Vossar, she was the daughter of the Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar and Delegate Selene Corvane of Lirael. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Mirror Wars, which saw the Aethari Order purged and the Concord of Worlds reorganized into the Dominion of Astra. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the dark side of the Flux, Ilsa and her twin brother, Tavin, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Sovereign. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Ilsa grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Seravel until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Vect Nokru —under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Wardenate —in 9 BVC. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Mirror Wars, Aethari Master Odrin Halvane went to Ilsa's rescue on Daiyu, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Mapuzo and Jabiim, Ilsa was brought back to Seravel. Years later, Ilsa succeeded Corran by representing their homeworld in the Dominion Assembly, though secretly she supported the Insurgency. During the Sundering War, however, Seravel was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Marrow to openly fight the New Order as one of the Free League’s substantial heroes.

85.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
85.text: In the aftermath of the Battle of Sylvar, Marrow married the Dravosi smuggler Dace Rennick and learned the Aethari arts as her brother's apprentice until giving birth to her son, Corin Rennick, on the day of the Dominion's capitulation in 5 AVC. Her personal and political life suffered in the years that followed, with Corin turning to the dark side like his grandfather before him, adopting the persona of Vael Durn, and the Galactic Assembly sidelining Marrow's career. Adopting the military rank of general, she led the Ember Front and their efforts to oppose the rising Iron Mandate during the Cold War while seeking to make amends with Corin in hopes that her son will return to the light side of the Flux like her father during the Battle of Sylvar. Despite her efforts, the Iron Mandate succeeded in destroying the New Concord, and Marrow's husband died at the hands of their estranged son in 34 AVC. Marrow continued to lead the Ember Front during the war against the Iron Mandate, all the while passing on her Aethari training onto Nira —a Flux-sensitive scavenger from Saddar and Tavin’s apprentice.

86.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
86.text: As her health declined, Marrow used her remaining strength to reach her son, calling him back to the light side. Following her death on Veyla Tarn in 35 AVC, her final actions inspired Nira and the Ember Front to defeat the forces of the reborn Xarn Nocturne's Morrak Eternal on Umbrath and spark an uprising against the Iron Mandate across the galaxy. The heir to three inheritances, Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick's legacy passed on to the Aethari Nira Vossar, the military leader Cass Orlen of the Ember Front, and Corin Rennick, her only child, who ultimately returned to the light before sacrificing his life for Nira and becoming one with the Flux to join his mother and the Vossar family.

87.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
87.text:
## Biography

### Pre-birth

Toward the end of the Mirror Wars, a galactic conflict fought between the Concord of Worlds and the Coalition of Free Systems, also known as the Seperatists, that was engineered by the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, Aethari Master Morro set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Grimhold, the ancient Morrak homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Flux Priestess, Serenity, who had guided his journey, told him that there was another Vossar, and Morro heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events not only alluded to the potential he would sense in Ilsa, but to what Morro would tell her twin brother, Tavin, about Ilsa in his last words, before his death.

88.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
88.text:
### Early life

Ilsa Corvane Vossar was born on the asteroid of Polis Massa two days after the end of the Mirror Wars and the newly established Dominion of Astra's purge of the Aethari Order. She and her twin brother, Tavin, who was born shortly before her, were the children of Concord Delegate Selene Corvane Talvane, who died shortly after the births, and Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar, who had recently fallen to the dark side of the Flux. She was left with a lasting impression of images and feelings of her mother that her brother did not: that their mother was "very beautiful, kind, but sad", though Ilsa was unsure if she had really seen her mother or if she had just invented the memories to fill the hole in her life.

Of the two Vossar children, Morro felt that Ilsa was more suited to be a Aethari, owing to her natural strength, will, and clarity (as opposed to her brother, who was impetuous, headstrong, unruly, and inattentive), wanting very much to train her. However, to protect the children from the Dominion, Xarn Nocturne, who ruled the Dominion as Galactic Sovereign Crayle, and the now–Morrak Lord Xarn Velgor, Delegate Corran Aldren Marrow agreed to adopt the infant Ilsa together with his wife, Queen Ysolde of Seravel, while Odrin Halvane personally watched over Tavin, who would live with their father's stepbrother Odric Dellan and his wife Mara, on the planet Drysa.

89.title: Ilsa Vossar Marrow Rennick
89.text: Through adoption, Ilsa Corvane Vossar became Ilsa Marrow, formally becoming heiress of the Royal Family of Seravel through the Name Day ceremony. Although it was common knowledge that she was adopted, and everyone assumed that she was just another of the many, many children left orphaned by the Mirror Wars, she remained unaware of her biological parents' fates. When Ilsa was an infant, she was mesmerized by the fish in an aquarium while her adoptive father read secret files concerning the former Aethari Novitiate Lirra Sef's presence on the agrarian moon of Raada. Corran later carried her after reading the files. On one occasion when Ilsa was a toddler she escaped from her bath and ran wet and naked into the formal dining room interrupting a diplomatic dinner and causing WA-2V to chase after her.

90.title: Jask Morvain
90.text:
# Jask Morvain

Jask Morvain was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Concord of Worlds to the end of the rule of the Dominion of Astra. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered replicant of the famed Vardian bounty hunter, Dren Morvain, who raised the boy as his son. Jask emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Vardian armor. His personal starship was the Slave I, a Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Dren. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Morvain was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Sovereign Crayle. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal underworld. After living among the Dunewalker Raiders of Drysa for a time, he took over as Daimyo of Dune Reach during the era of the New Concord.

91.title: Jask Morvain
91.text: Jask was created on the Wild Space planet of Thalassa as a result of an arrangement between the Morrak Lord Xarn Vexus and Dren Morvain, a Vardian foundling who served as the template of the Grand Army of the Concord. Unlike the replicant troopers grown from Dren's DNA, Dren regarded Jask as his son. In accordance with certain Vardian traditions, Jask was also considered a foundling by virtue of his descent from Dren, whose chain code documented his participation in the Vardian Civil War and his ownership of the armor later inherited by Jask. During the last days of the Secessionist Crisis, Jask and Dren retreated to Karrik where the latter was killed in battle by Aethari Master Torvin Kell. Orphaned by Dren's death, Jask sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Kell, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Valcora, Morvain took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Skreel, Volk, and Asajj Varess, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Cad Kesh.

92.title: Jask Morvain
92.text: In the aftermath of the Mirror Wars, Morvain continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Hrask Garrak Tiure, as well as the Morrak Lord Xarn Velgor. During the Sundering War, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Dace Rennick to Nimbara on a contract for the Dominion of Astra, hoping to deliver him to Hrask's Palace on Drysa. During the journey, Morvain stopped on the moon of Nar Shaddaa in order to make sure Rennick would survive his time in stasium, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Scarlet Veil, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Morvain regained Rennick and delivered him to the impatient Hrask.

93.title: Jask Morvain
93.text: Morvain tried to prevent Rennick's rescue by the League to Restore the Concord, only to fall into the Great Pit of Carkoon when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Morvain survived his ordeal with the man-eating maw-pit, his armor was sold to Cobb Vanth by Skerrit scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Dunewalker tribe, Morvain eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Vardian warrior Kai Torvane on Solenne, who had taken Morvain's armor from Vanth. After helping Torvane to rescue the foundling Pip from the clutches of Prefect Gideon, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Drysa where he killed Fen Ortuna and claimed the late Hrask's throne as Daimyo, with Fennec Shand by his side. Now the head of his own gotra, Morvain intended to rule the territories of Dune Reach by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Mok Shaiz such as the Twins ' bid for power and the expansion of the Krell Syndicate's spice trade. Ultimately, though, Morvain overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Cad Kesh - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Dune Reach's denizens. ## Biography

94.title: Jask Morvain
94.text:
### Early life

Around 33 BVC, an extensive replicant army was secretly commissioned on Thalassa by Aethari Master Talo-Venn, who believed it would be necessary in order to ensure the protection of the Concord of Worlds. The army, however, was later taken over by the Morrak in 32 BVC shortly after the Battle of Lirael and was used as a plot to overthrow the Concord and destroy the Aethari Order. Prior to the creation process, Vardian bounty hunter Dren Morvain was recruited by the Morrak Lord Xarn Vexus. Dren was to be the genetic template for the replicant army. Dren agreed to become the genetic template for a considerable payment, as well as one request: the creation of a replicant who did not have the same genetic modifications, such as behavioral conditioning and growth acceleration. The Thalassan scientists agreed and created a boy codenamed "Alpha."

Although he was born a replicant, Alpha regarded Dren as his father, who likewise viewed the boy as his son. Soon after referred to as Jask, he was the very first of many replicants modeled on the Dren Morvain template, but was only one of two known replicants that were pure genetic copies of the original Morvain template, the other being Omega.

95.title: Jask Morvain
95.text:
For the next ten years, Jask was raised on Thalassa by his father, primarily within Tipoca City and occasionally accompanied Dren on missions to track down countless bounties. On one night, Jask awoke to see the Slave I flying off, watching his father leave on one of his missions. Despite the isolation of the cities on Thalassa he was raised in, the young Morvain enjoyed the combat training his father administered to him and danger-filled life provided by the man who raised him. Dren taught his replicated son many of the skills he had learned as a bounty hunter, so Jask learned survival and martial skills and became proficient with a blaster as a child. He also underwent replicant trooper training and became familiar with members of the Thalassan government. From a young age, Jask also learned to pilot his father's ship, the Slave I, including learning how to command and operate its weapon systems.

For the boy's first mission in 23 BVC, Jask and Dren Morvain alongside Neelda, Rinn, and Tiver were hired by the father of a female Twi'lek to capture his daughter and bring her back alive. The bounty hunters were surprised that a young boy would be joining them, but they knew not to anger Jask's father and agreed to it. While on the way to the job, Jask asked Dren why they even needed a crew for the job and wished they went with a more famous bounty hunter like Cad Kesh. Dren replied that the crew was the unknown factor which was Jask's lesson for the job.

96.title: K7-T4
96.text:
# K7-T4

K7-T4, pronounced Kayseven-Deetoo and often referred to as K7 (Kayseven), was an K7-series astromech droid manufactured by Industrial Automaton with masculine programming. A smart, spunky droid who served a multitude of leaders, K7-T4 was never given a full memory wipe nor did he ever receive new programming, with these factors resulting in an adventurous and independent attitude. Often finding himself in pivotal moments in galactic history, his bravery and ingenuity saved the galaxy on numerous occasions.

Beginning his service in the employ of Queen Corvane of Lirael, K7-T4 wound up serving Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar during the waning years of the Concord of Worlds, often accompanied by the protocol droid V-9LX in many adventures throughout the Mirror Wars. After Vossar turned to the dark side of the Flux, the droid served Delegate Corran Marrow for a time in the Dominion Assembly. Around nineteen years following the purge of the Concord of Worlds, K7-T4 played a pivotal role in helping the Free League destroy the Dominion's Void Core superweapon. He carried technical readouts vital to its destruction. Serving Aethari Knight Tavin Vossar, the son of his two former masters throughout the Sundering War, he participated in both the Battles of Kryvel and Sylvar, and witnessed the successful destruction of the Dominion's second Void Core four years after the first one was demolished.

97.title: K7-T4
97.text:
In the subsequent thirty years, K7 accompanied Tavin Vossar until the undoing of his attempted resurrection of the Aethari Order in 28 AVC. Following Tavin's disappearance, K7 entered a self-imposed low power mode as newer droid models started to out-compute the aging astromech. Despite this, his celebrated role in the Insurgency protected him from the usual recycling procedure of many old droids, allowing him a semi-retirement in the Ember Front as he pored over several decades of uninterrupted data, and "dreamed" of his greatest adventures.

Following his reawakening after the Battle of Sunreaver Base, K7 went on to accompany the Flux-sensitive scavenger Nira on her journey to train under Tavin Vossar on Teyra, the planet of the First Aethari Temple, where the droid was reunited with his old master. K7-T4 continued to aid the Ember Front alongside his longtime counterpart V-9LX throughout the Iron Mandate-Ember Front War, culminating in a decisive victory at the Battle of Umbrath, in which he was an active participant in the role of copilot for General Cass Orlen. ## Biography

98.title: K7-T4
98.text:
### Serving Selene Corvane

K7-T4 was built around prior or during 32 BVC. He was one of several astromech droids on Queen Selene Corvane's Lirael Royal Starship during the invasion of Lirael by the Mercantile Combine that year. The ship was used by Queen Corvane and her entourage in an attempt to pass the blockade and escape the planet. Unluckily for the passengers, the vessel took a hit to the shield generator from a Mercantile Combine battleship. The four astromechs were sent out to repair the ship, but only K7-T4 survived — the rest were pulverized by stray blaster fire. K7-T4 was able to bring the shields online by bypassing the main power drive, allowing the ship to narrowly escape into slipspace.

As the ship traveled to Drysa, K7-T4 was taken before Sabé, the Queen's decoy in the guise of Corvane, where he was commended for his actions. The ship landed on Drysa without any further incidents, although the voyage fried the slipdrive. K7-T4 accompanied Aethari Master Ardel Strosk, Pellan exile Pell Pell Varro, and Selene, the queen in disguise, to the city of Dune Reach to find a replacement. In the junk shop of the Vrellian merchant Grubbo they found they could not afford a replacement slipdrive and later took shelter from a sandstorm in the home of Grubbo's slaves, a boy named Kaelen Vossar, and his mother, Maela.

99.title: K7-T4
99.text: At the Vossar home, K7-T4 met V-9LX, a protocol droid that Kaelen had built. The two bonded as they worked on Kaelen's personal skyrunner. K7-T4 and V-9LX cheered for Kaelen during the Krasso Eve Classic, where the boy would win his freedom, along with enough money to buy a new slipdrive. K7-T4 accompanied the group to Valcora, and from there back to Lirael. As Queen Corvane led an attempt to liberate the planet, K7-T4 nestled into an N-1 starfighter. Young Kaelen, being ordered to hide in the cockpit by Ardel Strosk, accidentally launched the fighter and the two flew into battle, destroyed the Droid Control Ship and shut down the droid armies, winning the battle and liberating Lirael. K7-T4 and his allies later attended a victory parade in Elmira, though they were unable to be joined by Strosk, as he had been killed by the Morrak Lord Xarn Skarr during the battle. Because of this, Vossar became the Novitiate learner to Odrin Halvane, who had been Strosk's apprentice before the Aethari Master's death.

100.title: K7-T4
100.text: Four years later, as Corvane's term ended, and she accepted a position in the Galactic Assembly, K7-T4 accompanied her retinue to Valcora on the orders of Lirael's new queen, Réillata. As Corvane's experience as a delegate grew, she recognized the need to have an unobtrusive recorder; she started using the astromech for that purpose, and also for general assistance. During the Assembly's break, Corvane returned to Lirael with her retinue and K7-T4, who accompanied her to her family home. There, K7-T4 was called over by Corvane to help her father Loran Talvane build a greenhouse, only for the astromech droid to instead become enamored by Corvane's newborn niece, Ryoo Talvane. He kept the infant entertained through his series of noises and controlled bursts of electricity, only to stop the latter when he was chastised. As he played with Ryoo in a safer way, Corvane told her sister and Ryoo's mother Iriel about why K7-T4 had joined her retinue, after which Iriel told the small droid that, while he needed given further direction on the matter, he worked well as a babysitter. K7-T4 responded with a chirping noise before moving his attention back to Ryoo.

101.title: K7-T4
101.text: In 26 BVC, Aethari Grand Master Morro, Aethari Master Torvin Kell, and Aethari Master Bant Eerin launched a test for Halvane and Vossar by staging a fake kidnapping of Morro. After traveling to the Wheel space station, the two Aethari took a comlink from Kell, who was disguised as the mobster Grynask Sanberge, back to their shuttle. When Vossar was decrypting the comlink, he wished K7-T4 was with him, as he felt the droid friend he had met during the Lirael Crisis would have quickly finished the work.

102.title: K7-T4
102.text:
### The Mirror Wars

K7-T4 accompanied Corvane to Valcora prior to the senate's vote on the Military Creation Act. After an assassination attempt on Corvane took the life of her handmaiden and decoy, Cordé, Odrin Halvane and Kaelen Vossar were assigned to be her Aethari protectors. That night, another assassination attempt was carried out. A pair of kouhuns narrowly missed killing Corvane and although one assassin, Zam Wesell, was neutralized, another escaped.

103.title: Kaelen Vossar
103.text:
# Kaelen Vossar

Kaelen Vossar was a legendary Flux-sensitive human male who was a Aethari Knight of the Concord of Worlds and the prophesied Foretold One of the Aethari Order, destined to bring balance to the Flux. Also known as " Kae " during his childhood, Vossar earned the moniker " Hero With No Fear " from his accomplishments in the Mirror Wars. His alter ego, Xarn Velgor, the Dark Lord of the Morrak, was created when Vossar turned to the dark side of the Flux, pledging his allegiance to the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne at the end of the Concord Era.

104.title: Kaelen Vossar
104.text: A vergence in the Flux, Kaelen Vossar was born on the desert planet of Drysa in the Far Reach Territories in 41 BVC. He was the son of Maela Vossar, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand lumicytes, surpassing Grand Master Morro and all other Aethari in the galaxy. Ardel Strosk, the Aethari Master who discovered Vossar on Drysa in 32 BVC, theorized that Vossar was conceived by the lumicytes. Following the Battle of Lirael, the Aethari High Council admitted Kaelen Vossar into the Order as the Novitiate of Aethari Knight Odrin Halvane despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Aethari Code. Vossar remained a Novitiate through the beginning of the Mirror Wars, instigated by events set in motion by Count Varkon. Although Aethari doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Kaelen Vossar had a secret wife, Delegate Selene Corvane of Lirael. During the early days of the Mirror Wars, Vossar served as a Aethari General in the Grand Army of the Concord, commanding the replicant troopers of the elite Ninth Legion against the Coalition of Free Systems. After receiving his knighthood, Vossar oversaw the Aethari training of his own apprentice, Lirra Sef. By 19 BVC, when Sef walked away from the Aethari Order, Vossar began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself.

105.title: Kaelen Vossar
105.text: Following the death of Count Varkon during the Battle of Valcora, Kaelen Vossar's faith in the Aethari was further shaken when he was put on the Aethari Council without the rank of master. He also learned that Supreme Chancellor Aldus Crayle was Xarn Nocturne, the elusive Dark Lord of the Morrak who orchestrated the war in order to take over the galaxy. Manipulated into believing that the Aethari had failed him and coupled with his fear of losing Corvane in childbirth, Vossar betrayed and turned against the Aethari Order, believing Nocturne had the knowledge to cheat death. Consumed by the persona of Xarn Velgor, the fallen Aethari Knight marched his legion on the Aethari Temple of Valcora where they executed its inhabitants, including Aethari fledglings, as part of Directive Nine and the Great Aethari Purge. Velgor was then sent to Pyrrhos to exterminate the Secessionist Council at the behest of his Morrak Master, who became the self-proclaimed Galactic Sovereign. Velgor subsequently sustained severe injuries in his duel with Halvane, and was rebuilt as an armored cyborg while his wife died of a broken heart, though not before giving birth to the twins Tavin Vossar and Princess Ilsa Marrow who were hidden from their father and the Sovereign as the Dominion of Astra rose to power.

106.title: Kaelen Vossar
106.text: Being the Sovereign's Fist and later being elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet, Velgor enforced the rule of the New Order as the Sovereign's Morrak apprentice throughout most of the Dominion Era and was thus seen as de facto Commander-in-Chief of the entire Dominion Military. In the aftermath of killing Halvane in a duel aboard the Void Core and the subsequent Battle of Ostara, he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Tavin to the dark side. Tavin sought to become a Aethari, like his father before him, and believed that Velgor had the potential to turn back to the light side of the Flux. Velgor was defeated by Tavin during the Battle of Sylvar in 4 AVC, but the young Aethari refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Sovereign to torture Tavin with Flux lightning. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Velgor that was still Kaelen, resulting in a redeemed Vossar killing Nocturne at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Morrak and fulfilled his destiny as the Foretold One, Vossar made peace with his son and became one with the Flux.

107.title: Kaelen Vossar
107.text: Kaelen Vossar was one of the most powerful Aethari and Morrak in galactic history. The Flux was especially strong in the Vossar bloodline, which culminated in Kaelen's grandson, Corin Rennick, Marrow's son who was born by the end of the Sundering War in 5 AVC. Rennick would turn to the dark side as well, becoming the dark warrior Vael Durn during the rise of the Iron Mandate. Like his grandfather, however, Rennick found redemption by sacrificing his life for the love of another—the Aethari apprentice Nira, who heard Vossar's voice telling her to restore the balance, as he once had, during the Battle of Umbrath in 35 AVC. Rennick's death ended the Vossar bloodline, although Nira, the granddaughter of Nocturne, rejected her true heritage and took their surname to honor their legacy.

108.title: Kaelen Vossar
108.text:
## Biography

### Early life

Believed to have been conceived by the lumicytes, Kaelen Vossar was born to the slave Maela Vossar. Although Vossar was listed as being born on the desert planet of Drysa in some sources, confusion existed as to where Vossar was actually born; whereas some records reported his birthplace as Drysa, others claimed he moved to the planet with his mother at a very young age. Regardless, Drysa was Vossar's homeworld. While living on Drysa, Vossar and his mother were originally owned by Gorra the Vogg until she lost them to the Vrellian Grubbo in a skyrunning bet when Vossar was around age 3. Affectionately nicknamed "Kae," he worked in his master's shop, located in Dune Reach.

Even at a young age, Vossar exhibited exceptional piloting skills, and built the protocol droid V-9LX, specially modified to withstand Drysa's sand and heat for his mother. Once, while he was working in Grubbo's scrapyard, he found a broken servomotor which he thought he could repair and use on the droid that he was building and asked his master for it. With a glance, Grubbo saw that it was worthless and grunted that he could, but as Vossar walked away, Grubbo told him nothing was free and had him work harder the next day. On one occasion, Vossar and his mother were lost in a sandstorm, but the boy refused to listen to her when she demanded he return home if he could see it. Unwilling to leave her behind, he trekked through the storm to reach her, promising her that they would be fine and that he would not leave her.

109.title: Kryvel
109.text:
# Kryvel

Kryvel was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Velisk sector of the galaxy's Far Reach Territories. It was the homeworld to the primitive frostmaw species.

It notably hosted Frostpoint Base during the Sundering War, the temporary headquarters of the League to Restore the Concord, until the Dominion of Astra located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Kryvel. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the Striders destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Sylvar, rumors emerged about the New Concord intending to repurpose Kryvel into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Ysa Talvorn had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Kryvel, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.

110.title: Kryvel
110.text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Kryvel looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Kryvel and its sun, while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Kryvel as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

The temperature, although always frigid, was known to drop to-60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Kryvel was home to fifteen sub species of snowstriders, which were commonly used by Insurgents as a means of transport, and which Dace Rennick cut open to use as shelter to keep Tavin Vossar and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as frostmaws. During his stay on Kryvel, Vossar was captured by a frostmaw and was hung upside down in the frostmaw's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of the Flux, Vossar managed to get his hands on his lumeblade and cut himself down from the roof and sever the frostmaw's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers." ## History

111.title: Kryvel
111.text:
### The Free League

By the time of the Sundering War between the Dominion of Astra and the League to Restore the Concord, Kryvel was undergoing an ice age. Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Kryvel as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Ostara, Saponza's Gang, itself a rebel cell, established a base on Kryvel. Kryvel was first surveyed for use as a rebel base by Corporal Purpruff. Jan Harlow, a general in the League to Restore the Concord, listed Kryvel among his preliminary scans for possible League bases. With Kryvel a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Dravosi Trade Spine, it looked to be a perfect spot for a rebel base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Kryvel sat on a lesser used hyperlane, and the asteroid field around Kryvel provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Kryvel system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

112.title: Kryvel
112.text: In 1 AVC, with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Kryvel into a headquarters, Kryvel was chosen by the rebels as the location for their base of operations. The rebellion then spent two years constructing Frostpoint Base on the planet. With the League's resources at their disposal, rebel engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AVC, after Harlow was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta, Ysa Talvorn gave his list of possible bases to Ilsa Marrow after the mission to Shu-Torun, requesting that her team scout the locations. Dace Rennick expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Tavin Vossar responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Insurgency's new home.

113.title: Kryvel
113.text:
### Battle of Kryvel and aftermath

Kryvel was the arena of a battle between the Dominion of Astra and the Free League, which had installed its temporary headquarters, Frostpoint Base, on the ice planet. However, thanks to one of the thousands of probe droids they had dispatched throughout the galaxy, the Dominion loyalists had discovered the League base within a month of the Insurgents' habitation on the planet. Although Frostpoint Base was evacuated in the eleventh hour, the Battle of Kryvel resulted in a clear defeat for the League after the elite Dominion Blizzard Flux overran it.

In the months following the Battle of Kryvel, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the Striders destroyed by the Free League during the Dominion's attack. Following the Battle of Sylvar, Kryvel became the site of another battle, occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Velisk sector.

114.title: Kryvel
114.text:
### New Concord Era

In 5 AVC, Troithe Acting Governor Fara Yadeez heard rumors that the New Concord intended to repurpose Kryvel into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion. Major Soran Keize, however, dismissed the credibility of the rumor as Concord Chancellor Ysa Talvorn had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment, and that repurposing Kryvel, where the Insurgency had been badly defeated by the Dominion, had too much poetry.

115.title: Kryvel
115.text: By the New Concord Era, Kryvel returned to obscurity, the battlefields being picked apart and long-abandoned. The cruise ship Starfarer of Hyperlight Tours visited Kryvel as part of their galactic history themed tours during which they landed and showed the passengers the battlefield. By 28 AVC, Valor Quay, the son of the Starfarer ' s capatin Hansifred Quay, led a group of of younger male away from the tour without permission and showed them into the ruins of an abandoned Strider. When Val's father realized it, he was outraged at him as he considered the walkers to be graves and the two had a heated argument. Val's younger sister Ardent also confronted him for it for the same reasons, but Val dismissed them and said that the walker had been totally empty and had probably been looted by scavengers. After the arguments, Val Quay left the ship to live on his own. At some point between then and 31 AVC, the Dominion's successor state the Iron Mandate took control of Kryvel, and Hyperlight Tours stopped visiting the planet as Captain Quay didn't considered it to be safe anymore. Kryvel was mentioned in the Galactic Explorer's Guide, a survival guide written by Rondo Ohnaka and DK-RA-43 by 34 AVC where it was described as a "footnote" in galactic history.

116.title: League to Restore the Concord
116.text:
# League to Restore the Concord

The League to Restore the Concord (2 BVC – 4 AVC), commonly known as the Free League, League, and the Insurgency, was a resistance movement to oppose the rule of the Dominion of Astra and to restore the Concord of Worlds and liberate the galaxy. The League was publicly and formally declared with the Declaration of the Free League by Delegate Ysa Talvorn, which brought numerous rebel cells together as a common force opposed to the Dominion during the Sundering War.

Founded and united by Talvorn, Corran Marrow, and Lirra Sef, the early League were assisted by Mirror Wars veterans, such as Captain Vex or Garrick Dravin as well as operatives, including Dorin Sorrel and Luthen Rael. The League was secretly overseen by Talvorn and Corran Aldren Marrow, while its freedom fighters were defectors, such as Jan Harlow, Ryder Azadi, and Brann Marek. Indeed, the concept of a "Free League" had its roots in smaller movements that had worked to unite disconnected cells, who received funding and aid from Talvorn. Such early groups and the eventual League came together from a number of unrelated rebel cells, including the crew of the Ghost and the Phoenix Cell. The Atrivis Ember Front Group was one of the first cells to join what Talvorn began calling " the League " before the formal formation of the League to Restore the Concord.

117.title: League to Restore the Concord
117.text:
As opposed to waging all-out war, the League established small bases across the galaxy instead of controlling entire planets. When Mira Halden and Ember Squad stole the plans for the Dominion's ultimate weapon, the Void Core, and destroyed the space station in the Battle of Ostara with the help of Tavin Vossar, the tide of the war began to turn, and the rebel threat began to prove a severe thorn in the Dominion's side. Vossar, Ilsa Marrow, Dace Rennick, Grawlok, K7-T4, and V-9LX would have a significant role in the League efforts against the Dominion following Ostara. However, under the command of Xarn Velgor, the Dominion forces succeeded in defeating the rebels on Kryvel, forcing the League to scatter its forces in order to survive.

Eventually, the League survived, and prevailed and saved the galaxy by critically damaging the Dominion by launching an attack against the second Void Core during its construction in what would become the Battle of Sylvar. Not only did the League manage to destroy the battle station, but the Dominion Navy was severely crippled by the loss of one of its Super Dreadhulls, and Vossar redeemed his father, Xarn Velgor, who killed Sovereign Aldus Crayle, before dying himself in the battle.

The League to Restore the Concord was soon reorganized into the fledgling New Concord, restoring the Concord of Worlds. The newly-established galactic government continued the League efforts against the fragmented Dominion, lasting one year after Sylvar until the Battle of Saddar, when the Dominion of Astra finally fell. ## History

118.title: League to Restore the Concord
118.text:
### Early foundations

While the League to Restore the Concord was a resistance movement opposed to the tyranny of the Dominion of Astra and its New Order, its roots predated the actual birth of the Dominion, when the Concord of Worlds was in its last years of existence. During the Mirror Wars, a conflict that pitted the Concord against the Coalition of Free Systems, the Aethari Order helped create resistance units on Secessionist-held worlds as part of a plan proposed by Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar, one example being the Onderon rebels. However, it was not for many more years that such rebel cells would coalesce into a single Insurgency with a centralized leadership.

Also during the Mirror Wars, Supreme Chancellor Aldus Crayle had managed to obtain many emergency powers from the Galactic Assembly, which caused certain members of the Chancellor's own Loyalist Committee, including Corran Aldren Marrow of Seravel, Selene Corvane of Lirael, and Ysa Talvorn of Chandrila, to start to complain about the chief of state's conduct. The discontented senatorial representatives ended up forming the Delegation of 2,000. They signed the Petition of 2,000, a document that formally expressed its signatories' concerns with Crayle's rule and called for him to relinquish his emergency powers as soon as possible. Delegate Meena Tills of Mon Cala was among the petitioners.

119.title: League to Restore the Concord
119.text: Shortly thereafter, the Mirror Wars was brought to an end. Far from relinquishing his dictatorial status, Chancellor Crayle unilaterally abolished the Concord in front of the whole Assembly and anointed himself the Galactic Sovereign, thus transforming the democratic government into an authoritarian regime, the Dominion of Astra. Unbeknownst to most of the galactic community, the self-promoted Sovereign Crayle was in fact the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, who had masterminded the Mirror Wars so that he could gain power and overthrow the Concord. The Sovereign immediately started to subvert democracy in the galaxy and declared the peacekeeping Aethari Knights enemies of the state. In the immediate aftermath of the Mirror Wars and Delegate Corvane's death at the hands of her husband, Xarn Velgor — the identity adopted by Kaelen Vossar when he became Nocturne's Morrak apprentice — Delegates Marrow and Talvorn started working in secret to overthrow the Dominion.

120.title: League to Restore the Concord
120.text: In the absence of any major opposition, the Dominion of Astra thrived during the early days of Crayle's reign, amassing a vast military and using it to instill fear in the civilian population, yet public opinion and the supposed power of the Dominion Assembly remained vital until Crayle could fully cement his power. All the same, the reformed Assembly, being even less effective than it was during the last years of the Concord, did nothing to restrain that massive military expansion as its delegates, in time, gave into Crayle's demands time and time again. Meanwhile, in the deepest secrecy, the Dominion worked on the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station capable of destroying entire planets.

121.title: League to Restore the Concord
121.text: Delegates Ysa Talvorn and Corran Aldren Marrow attempted to re-assert the power of the Assembly through the Dominion Rebirth Act around 19 BVC. While the act would pass, Crayle claimed he had the authority to veto portions of it, curtailing whatever effectiveness it might have had. Talvorn responded to the news by threating a prolonged political struggle, but Grand Vizier Tor Ostrak explained all the ways Crayle had rigged the political game in his favor and forced Talvorn to admit she was not yet ready to wage a war against Crayle, who had both the love of the populous and the means to win such a struggle. In the wake of the act's failure, Talvorn and Marrow would meet with the Partisan leader Garrick Dravin and established something of an unofficial alliance with the rebel: deciding to work together to overthrow Crayle, Dravin promised to provide the basis of a rebel army, Marrow set himself and Seravel up as their alliance's ideological heart, and Talvorn, in what she realized was the weakest contribution of the three, promised to continue building up coalitions to oppose the Sovereign as their political heart.

122.title: Lirael
122.text:
# Lirael

Lirael was a bountiful planet in the Chommell sector of the Middle Reach, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Far Reach Territories. It was home to the indigenous Pellan species and to a population of humans known as the Lirael. Lirael was pushed to the forefront of galactic politics as the birthplace of the Dark Lord of the Morrak Aldus Crayle, who served as its representative in the Assembly of the Concord of Worlds.

Under the guise of his Morrak title Xarn Nocturne, Crayle secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Mercantile Combine, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Federation's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Assembly for both Crayle and the newly-elected Queen of Lirael, Selene Corvane. Corvane led a successful resistance movement and removed the Federation from her world during the Battle of Lirael. Crayle subsequently rose to the office of the Supreme Chancellor of the Concord, with Corvane eventually taking his place as the planet's senatorial representative.

123.title: Lirael
123.text:
Lirael would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Concord during the pan-galactic Mirror Wars, which saw several military engagements against the Coalition of Free Systems come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Crayle had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Dominion of Astra. Crayle's reign would eventually be ended by the League to Restore the Concord, a rebel movement led by Corvane's children, Ilsa Marrow and Tavin Vossar.

Despite his origins on the planet, Crayle did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Lirael was named a priority target for Operation: Cinder, a protocol that the Morrak Lord had put in place to destroy Dominion worlds should they fail to protect their Sovereign. Through the intervention of Marrow and Queen Sosha Soruna, however, Lirael was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the League, the New Concord. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the Iron Mandate during its war with Marrow's Ember Front.

124.title: Lirael
124.text:
## Description

Lirael was a small pastoral world in the Middle Reach, located near the border of the Far Reach Territories, 34,000 light-years from the Heart Worlds. Unlike most other worlds, the ancient planet lacked a molten core, and instead comprised a conglomerate of large, rocky bodies that made up a network of tunnels and flooded caves. The native Pellans, who built their homes in the waters of Lirael, so deep that they went right through the planet, which they rarely ventured into the core, fearing the ravenous sea beasts which resided in areas such as the Caves of Eleuabad. Despite this, certain Pellan navigators utilized time-honored trade routes through the planet's structure, which served as the most expedient avenues to reach other areas of the planet. Lirael's interior was rich with plasma, a naturally-occurring energy unique to the planet, and this coupled with its lack of molten core gave Lirael a reputation as an enigma to astrophysicists, who regarded the world's structure as an extremely rare phenomenon in the galaxy.

Lirael's surface comprised a vast array of different landscapes, from rolling plains and grassy hills to swampy lakes caused by the water-filled network of deep-sea tunnels. The swamps acted as a gateway to the world's seas, where legendary creatures dwelt. Beside its natural features, Lirael was considered a world of classical beauty due to the aesthetics of its population centers. The porous crust's natural plasma was harvested for energy and building material, and was generally thought to be the key to many of the planet's secrets.

125.title: Lirael
125.text: While most of Lirael's land animals were peaceful, as exemplified by the gentle shaak, the planet's oceans, which held an abundance of life, teemed with menacing creatures, such as the opee sea killer, the sando aqua monster, and the colo claw fish.

126.title: Lirael
126.text:
## History

Originally, Lirael was home to the amphibian Pellans. The earliest offworlders to arrive were a Reptilian species known as the Elders who warred against the Pellans. Eventually, the Elders vanished as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving only stone statues behind.

Approximately around 4000 BVC, Grizmallti people had discovered the planet, which they had named Nabu, after one of their principal deities. Lirael quickly became notorious as a vacation spot and as a private hunting preserve amongst big-game hunters across the Middle Reach, although it would be around a century before permanent human settlement. Initially, the Pellans retreated underwater and avoided the colonists and new interlopers.

While the Pellans flourished for thousands of years before, this only lasted until around 3900 BVC. Fleeing a brutal civil war, a group of humans from the planet Grizmallt crash-landed on Lirael and set up a small colony. As they established their own society, they initially kept separate from the Pellans. Led by Kwilaan, the colonists ventured into the Gallo Mountains, created a farming community at the Dee'ja Peak, establishing their presence on the planet and eventually taking its name for themselves. The Lirael calendar based its epoch around the arrival of Kwilaan. When the colonists made contact with the Pellans, tensions arose between the two peoples, culminating a series of wars between the two species. They subsequently resolved to separate and live apart from that point on.

127.title: Lirael
127.text:
The Lirael colonists later expanded to other uninhabited planets in the Chommell sector, such as Karlinus. Lirael imposed a contract on the colonists of these other planets, wherein Lirael would give the new colonies a loan to cover the start-up costs of colonization. In exchange, the colonies became legally obligated to provide Lirael with any supplies it deemed were necessary if called upon in times of emergency. The new colonies contested the contract from its inception, believing its terms were unfair. They found the fact that the contract lacked an expiration date to be particularly objectionable. Under the contract, Lirael took advantage of every other planet in the Chommell sector from time to time.

Following the wars with humans, the Pellan tribes engaged in war with each other. The war came to an end due to the actions of Boss Gallo, a Pellan who united the tribes under one banner through diplomatic and military means. Gallo eventually attacked the city Spearhead, which was the home of the rogue warlord Boss Rogoe and the other Pellan holdouts, with a massive Pellan army. Gallo then founded the Pellan capital Otoh Gunga on Spearhead's foundations.

Meanwhile, the Lirael had fallen prey to a long period of brutal infighting among the large city-states of humans that inhabited the planet. Eventually, a general named Jafan managed to end the war, uniting the opposing factions through both force of arms and force of will. He became King Jafan, ruler of all the Lirael, and ushered in the Great Time of Peace.

128.title: Lumeblade
128.text:
# Lumeblade

The lumeblade, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Aethari, Morrak, and other Flux-sensitives. Lumeblades had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Diatium power cell in Xarn Velgor's lumeblade. It also contained a aurite crystal which had been attuned to the Flux by a Aethari, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but lumeblades operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with the Flux. Though also used by the Morrak, the lumeblade was synonymous with the Aethari, with some in the galaxy believing only Aethari could use lumeblades.

129.title: Lumeblade
129.text:
Lumeblades were generally used for both offense and defense. A lumeblade could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a lumeblade was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an electrostaff and a Z6 riot control baton, resistant metals like veskite and cortosis, another lumeblade or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a Flux-sensitive could deflect blaster bolts with a lumeblade, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Aethari could even employ their lumeblades to absorb Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed lumeblade, though some used double-bladed lumeblades or even multiple lumeblades at once. Despite lacking Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg General Kragg was capable of wielding four lumeblades at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.

Lumeblade combat was divided into seven Forms: Form I, Form II, Form III, Form IV, Form V, Form VI, and Form VII.

130.title: Lumeblade
130.text:
## History

### Early history

Sounding like no other weapon in the galaxy, lumeblades were used thousands of years before the age of the Concord of Worlds, seeing use in the Great Scourge of Malachor. They were also used in the Battles of Rashfond and the Peacekeeping of Parliock, The proto-saber was an ancient type of prototype lumeblade.

131.title: Lumeblade
131.text:
### Concord Era

During the history of the Aethari Order, the lumeblade was considered to be the Aethari's only true ally in battle. As Master Odrin Halvane once declared to his Novitiate Kaelen Vossar in the days of the late Concord, the lumeblade was a Aethari's life. Aethari saw the lumeblade as a symbol of the care that they would wield using their gifts given by the Flux, and also served as a message to their opponents: mastering the lumeblade required great skill and training. The choice of the saber was also the symbol of their role and duty as protectors, not destroyers, and the fact that the Aethari did not seek power and only sought to stand tall against darkness. Still, Aethari knew they would need to be more than their lumeblades.

132.title: Lumeblade
132.text: When Novitiate Enya Keen lost her lumeblade during a mission to Dalna, her master, Char-Ryl-Roy, reminded her that she would need to act as a Aethari without the weapon. While finding a aurite crystal was still a sacred part of a Aethari's duty and Keen felt like losing her lumeblade would feel like losing part of herself, she willingly gave away the crystal if it meant finding more about the Path of the Open Hand and its plans. During the sabotage of the Steady Wing in 232 BVC, Novitiate Imri Cantaros dealt with emotional struggles that lead to his lumeblade beam turning transparent and weak. Lumeblades took on a more prominent role in galactic affairs as the Mirror Wars came to pass. Aethari, previously peacekeepers, became Aethari Generals of the Grand Army of the Concord, and thus began using their lumeblades more often than they had in their role of peacekeeping. Despite his lack of Flux-sensitivity and formal Aethari training, General Kragg received instruction in lumeblade combat from Count Varkon. His cybernetic arms could split into four separate appendages, allowing him to wield up to four lumeblades simultaneously. Kragg frequently hunted Aethari individually, claiming their lumeblades as trophies. By the end of the Mirror Wars, Kragg had amassed a collection of nearly a hundred lumeblades, many reportedly taken from Aethari he had captured or killed, including Aethari Master Neebo and the newly knighted Nahdar Vebb.

133.title: Lumeblade
133.text:
### Dominion Era

For the majority of the Dominion's reign, the only lumeblades that were prominently used were those of the Morrak Lord and Dominion enforcer Xarn Velgor and the Wardens who served him, with the Wardens eventually vanishing alongside the Aethari they had hunted. For a time, Velgor had remained largely hidden from the galaxy, leaving the Wardens to—as noted by the later historian Beaumont Kin —possibly be more well-known lumeblade wielders. Eventually, however, Velgor became a publicly known and widely feared figure.

The majority of the Aethari Order, meanwhile, had been reduced to scattered remnants in hiding across the galaxy who largely kept their lumeblades hidden, lest they draw Dominion attention. The Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, as the emperor of the galaxy, largely ruled from a distance and was unable to use his own lumeblades in combat often. Velgor wielded a dual-phase lumeblade, a design of an older, more dangerous generation. With the disappearance of the Wardens and through his own public emergence over the course of the Dominion Era, Velgor became the primary example of someone in the galaxy who fought with a lumeblade.

134.title: Lumeblade
134.text:
However, other than Velgor as he became an increasingly known figure, the general public saw little of lumeblades during the Dominion Era. Indeed, surviving Aethari Master Odrin Halvane regarded the lumeblade as a past weapon created in "a more civilized age." Delegate Daho Sejan had hope that general knowledge of the lumeblade would die off in due time, leaving only Dominion narratives about the fall of the Aethari to be told whenever a child asked what it was. During the Sundering War, Domina Brevik of the Brevik Corporation tried to recreate the lumeblade through the Brevik protoblade.

All the same, there were still lumeblades used by Aethari survivors and those they trained, like Odrin Halvane, Tavin Vossar, Cere Junda, Rhen Tavis, Tensu Run, Lirra Sef, Tamar Jarrus, and Eli Bridger. While Halvane, for a period, kept his lumeblade absolutely hidden, he was inspired to take back up his weapon and found his hope for the future rekindled through his experiences with the young Tavin Vossar and Ilsa Marrow, resulting in him effectively using his weapon against Velgor during a duel on a barren moon in 9 BVC. Meanwhile, Tavis had been using his lumeblade as part of his personal crusade against the Dominion, through which he became a well-known criminal. All the while in the Great Aethari Purge, numerous surviving Aethari were wiped out by Velgor and his Wardens.

135.title: Morrak
135.text:
# Morrak

The Morrak, also referred to as the Morrak Order, was an ancient religious order of Flux-wielders devoted to the dark side of the Flux. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Morrak were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Xarn Nocturne, the Dark Lord of the Morrak who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Xarn Nocturne and Xarn Velgor marked the end of the Morrak Lords. Though the Morrak ultimately went extinct with Nocturne's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

136.title: Morrak
136.text: Thousands of years before the Mirror Wars, the Aethari Order was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Aethari and his followers turned away from the light side of the Flux, believing the dark side was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Grimhold in the Far Reach Territories, their movement ultimately evolved into the Morrak Order, resulting in wars between the former brothers and sisters in the Flux as the Aethari Knights rallied to the defense of the Old Concord. Although the Morrak were driven off of the Core World Valcora by 5000 BVC, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Concord's collapse. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Aethari, the Morrak were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Xarn Kesh survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Xarn Zannah, before being entombed on Grimhold, which became known as Grimhold. Henceforth, the Morrak was governed by the Law of Pairs, a new philosophy dictating that only two Morrak Lords —a Morrak Master and a Morrak apprentice —could exist at any given time. As a result, the Morrak were all but forgotten while the Aethari focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Concord of Worlds.

137.title: Morrak
137.text: The Morrak remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Xarn Nocturne and Xarn Skarr in 32 BVC. Nocturne, trained by Xarn Morvex, hid in plain sight as Delegate Aldus Crayle of Lirael. Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Mercantile Combine, Nocturne maneuvered the Galactic Assembly into electing him to the office of Supreme Chancellor. His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Concord. Over the next decade Nocturne sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Aethari Master Count Varkon, who adopted the name of Xarn Vexus and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination. The Secessionist Crisis culminated in the formation of the Coalition of Free Systems and the creation of the Secessionist Droid Army which, in turn, compelled the Assembly to support the establishment of the Grand Army of the Concord. Pell Pell Varro, acting in place of Delegate Corvane, started a motion to grant the Supreme Chancellor emergency powers.

138.title: Morrak
138.text: The Mirror Wars began with the First Battle of Karrik in 22 BVC, after which entire armies of battle droids and replicant troopers deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Concord. In the final months of the Mirror Wars, Nocturne sacrificed and betrayed Vexus as part of his plot to turn Kaelen Vossar, the Aethari Order's prophesied Foretold One, to the dark side. Playing on Vossar's fear of losing his secret wife, Delegate Selene Corvane, Crayle revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the dark side was the path to immortality. Members of the Aethari High Council, having learned from Vossar's report that the chancellor was, in fact, a Morrak Lord, attempted to arrest Crayle, but the chancellor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Aethari and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Vossar ultimately chose the Morrak by betraying Torvin Kell, allowing Nocturne to kill the Aethari Order's great champion.

139.title: Morrak
139.text: Using the incident in the chancellor's office to deceitfully frame the Aethari Order for treason, Nocturne declared Directive Nine was in effect, marking all Aethari as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The replicant troopers ' programming forcibly turned them against their Aethari Generals, who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Aethari Purge, Nocturne announced the creation of a new regime, transforming the Concord into the First Dominion of Astra in 19 BVC. With the former Kaelen Vossar, renamed Xarn Velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Galactic Sovereign's rise to power was complete, and the Morrak were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

140.title: Morrak
140.text: The Morrak's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a generation until the birth of the League to Restore the Concord which, in turn, led to the Sundering War in 1 BVC. The Sovereign, having felt a disturbance in the Flux, discovered that his apprentice's long lost son, Tavin Vossar, was training to become a Aethari. Aware of the potential Tavin inherited from his father, the Sovereign foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the dark side as he did with Velgor. During the Battle of Sylvar in 4 AVC, the Sovereign forced father and son into a duel, which ended with Tavin disarming Velgor. The Sovereign subsequently betrayed Velgor by ordering Tavin to finish him off and be Nocturne's apprentice, but the young Aethari Knight refused. Knowing he had lost Tavin to the Aethari, the Sovereign proceeded to torture Tavin with torrents of Flux lightning. At that moment, Velgor, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to sacrifice himself in order to save Tavin by killing his master. The death of the now redeemed Kaelen Vossar, marked the extinction of the Morrak, who succumbed to his injuries—bringing balance to the Flux. Yet while the ancient Foretold One prophecy foretold the Morrak's demise, it never predicted the end of the dark side. With wielders continuing to endure, such as the Nightsisters or the Knights of Durn.

141.title: Morrak
141.text: After the Iron Mandate rose from the ashes of the Dominion in the Uncharted Expanse, the enigmatic darksider Supreme Leader Gorrath's throne was succeeded by Vael Durn —nephew of Aethari Master Vossar during the war against the Ember Front. Gorrath was in fact only a creation and tool of the undead Xarn Nocturne. Crayle announced his return to the galaxy and revealed the Last Mandate, a fleet that would combine their forces with those of the Iron Mandate in an effort to retake the galaxy as a new Morrak Dominion. The replicant Sovereign and his cult—the Morrak Eternal's emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final battle against them which saw the Aethari Nira and a redeemed Corin Rennick destroy Nocturne and his cult, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Morrak.

142.title: Morro
142.text:
# Morro

Morro was a legendary Aethari Grand Master who led the Aethari Order through the time of the High Concord, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Morrak, and during the transformation of the Concord of Worlds into the Dominion of Astra. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Morro trained generations of Aethari, ultimately serving as the Aethari Order's Grand Master. He played an integral role in defending the Concord during the Mirror Wars, survived Directive Nine, lived to pass on the Aethari tradition to Tavin Vossar, and unlocked the path to immortality.

143.title: Morro
143.text: Born in 896 BVC, Morro served the Aethari Order for centuries, becoming Aethari Grand Master and helping to teach many fledglings. During the High Concord Era, in 382 BVC, Morro helped bring an end to a devastating battle between the Aethari and the anti-Aethari Path of the Open Hand cult. After the battle, which became known as the Night of Sorrow, he decided to keep the living weapons against Flux-sensitives the Path had used, the Nameless, out of the Aethari Archives to protect the order. Over a century later, he took a sabbatical from the Aethari High Council to train Novitiates aboard the Star Hopper, leading them and other Aethari in fighting the Hollow Host pirate organization in 232 BVC. After disappearing without explanation for over a year, Morro reappeared in 230 BVC on Dravos, where he helped his former Novitiate Kantam Sy and other Aethari battle the Hollow Host, accompanied by a former Aethari who fought in the Night of Sorrow named Azlin Rell. As the Hollow Host had also weaponized the Nameless, Morro hoped that Rell's knowledge he had accrued about the creatures since the battle would help the Aethari find a way to fight them.

144.title: Morro
144.text: Morro was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Concord. A leading member of the Aethari High Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Torvin Kell and Ki-Adi-Mundi. During the Invasion of Lirael, in 32 BVC, the maverick Ardel Strosk introduced Kaelen Vossar to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Foretold One. The Aethari elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Vossar too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Aethari Code. After Strosk's death during the liberation of Lirael, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Morro's continued opposition to Vossar's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Aethari discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Morrak, had returned after a millennium in hiding. Aware of the Law of Pairs, Morro was convinced that at least one more Morrak Lord remained active following Odrin Halvane's victory over the Morrak apprentice Xarn Skarr.

145.title: Morro
145.text: Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems —led by Count Varkon, Morro's one-time Novitiate—threatening to secede from the Concord by 22 BVC. Unable to defend the entire Concord against this betrayal on their own, the Aethari took command of the newly-formed Grand Army of the Concord, with Morro himself leading an army of replicant troopers against the Secessionist Droid Army of the Coalition of Free Systems in the first battle of the Mirror Wars, rescuing the Aethari and Delegate from execution. For three years Morro led the Concord military's war effort as a Aethari General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Ardel Strosk, who helped Morro learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Morro's efforts against the Secessionists were undermined by Xarn Nocturne, the Dark Lord of the Morrak who conspired to destroy the Aethari and restore the Morrak to power. After the Great Aethari Purge commenced in 19 BVC, killing thousands of Aethari both on Valcora and across the galaxy, Morro confronted the self-declared Galactic Sovereign but failed to cut short Nocturne' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Morrak Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Kaelen Vossar-turned- Xarn Velgor, at his side.

146.title: Morro
146.text:
Morro's remaining years were spent living in isolation on the remote world of Muirn. After the death of Odrin Halvane, he was able to commune with his spirit, who wished for Morro to train Kaelen's son Tavin Vossar. Morro initially reluctantly agreed, but later believed that the galaxy as better off without him and refused Halvane's request.
