After being convinced by Halvane to enter the Cave of Evil, in which he confronted many figures from his past and made peace with his failures, he agreed to teach Tavin Vossar, who soon after sought out the legendary Grand Master in the hope of becoming a Aethari Knight. He trained Vossar for a time, until despite Morro's warnings Vossar hurriedly abandoned his training to save his friends after a having a vision that they were in danger. A year later, in 4 AVC, with his health rapidly declining, Morro died of old age when Vossar returned to see him. He became one with the Flux, shortly before Tavin redeemed his father Kaelen, who fulfilled his destiny as the Foretold One by killing Nocturne.

Years later, Tavin Vossar's attempt to reform the Aethari Order would be foiled when his nephew Corin Rennick turned to the dark side and destroyed his Aethari Temple. Believing the galaxy was better without him and the Aethari, Vossar went into exile, just as Morro had. After his student he reluctantly trained, the scavenger Nira, also abandoned her training, Morro appeared as a ghost to Vossar. Morro taught Vossar to learn from his failures and helped him forgive himself. ## Biography

147.title: Morro
147.text:
### Early life

Born nine-hundred years before the Battle of Sylvar, Morro belonged to an ancient and mysterious species and little was known of Morro's early life; he never revealed his homeworld. As he was keenly attuned to the Flux, he joined the Aethari Order as a fledgling. As a Aethari Initiate, Morro made use of a training lumeblade. After undergoing the ritual known as the Gathering, he received his own personal aurite crystal, and Professor Oldbolt helped him construct his first lumeblade aboard the Crucible. The circumstances surrounding Morro and the construction of his first lumeblade were exciting, according to Oldbolt. At some point during his time as a fledgling, Morro skipped across the lily pads in the Aethari Temple's meditation pond.

148.title: Morro
148.text: Although Morro spoke little of his early days, it was rumored that one of his early instructors was the Hysalrian N'Kata Del Gormo. Morro was paired up with a personal mentor at a younger age than usual. During their time together, Morro's Aethari Master told him the tale of K'ungfu and Chuang, two great Aethari of the past. As a Novitiate, Morro visited multiple planets and during his first years he could have named them all, but in the following centuries, he couldn't remember how many he'd seen and later estimated the number to be in the tens of thousands. Around the age of one hundred, in 796 BVC, Morro was ready to pass on what he had learned. Having attained the rank of Master, he spent the next eight centuries training and tutoring generations of Aethari. It was estimated that over his lifetime, he trained around twenty thousand Aethari.

149.title: Muirn
149.text:
# Muirn

Muirn was a remote, unexplored planet in the Muirn system, and one of the purest places in the galaxy within the Flux. A remote world of swamps and forests, it served as a refuge for Aethari Grand Master Morro during his exile after the destruction of the Aethari Order. Tavin Vossar received advanced training in the ways of the Flux under Aethari Master Morro on Muirn, and it was later the place of Morro's death and transformation into the Flux.

150.title: Muirn
150.text:
## Description

Muirn was a planet located in the Sluis sector of the Far Reach Territories. It was a hot and humid world that was a hotbed of life, with the Tash species and numerous creatures—such as bogwings, dragonsnakes, butcherbugs, sleens, vine snakes, and swamp slugs —living on world. Aethari Master Morro would also make a home for himself on Muirn during his exile. Muirn was a mysterious, mist-shrouded, swampy planet, mostly covered in swamps and bogs, interspersed with countless shallow lakes and lagoons and multiple living caves. The continental and oceanic crusts of Muirn were only vaguely defined, and there was little in the way of volcanic activity or earthquakes. Examples of flora included the lahdia plant, the yoghurt plant, gnarltree, and yarum seed. The planet was devoid of any cities.

Among the purest locations in the entire galaxy within the energy field known as the Flux, it shared a mysterious time-related quality with such locales as Mortis and Teyra. The Cave of Evil was a vergence aligned with the dark side of the Flux on Muirn. The Cave was able to expand its influence across Muirn until Morro's arrival, which created a powerful presence in the light side of the Flux that kept the Cave in check. As such, during the Dominion Era, Muirn's ecosystem saw balance until Morro's passing, which the Cave took advantage of to spread its darkness across Muirn once more.

151.title: Muirn
151.text: Muirn had two seasons, a dry season and a wet season. During the peak of the long dry season (over half an orbit after the rains end) the uplands become too hot for most lifeforms to survive, necessitating any that live there to migrate to the lower lands. Beneath the rapidly leafing canopies of the gnarltrees that emerge from the receding green and thick waters, the once-inundated lowlands revert back to a marshy swamp once again. As the air grows more humid, the gray overcast clouds return and before another quarter orbit passes the planet is far enough away from its sun that the dry season ends and the rains return, again flooding the lowlands and covering the trees in water, making the uplands habitable once more.

152.title: Muirn
152.text:
## History

### Concord Era

During the High Concord Era, an academic paper was written that described Muirn as a world strong in the Flux.

During the Concord Era, Halka Four-Den Alpha Team was dispatched to the planet Muirn in order to chart and map the extending borders of the Concord of Worlds and learn more about it flora and fauna. After three months, Four-Den and her Alpha Team were overwhelmed by diseases, dangerous wildlife, and fast-growing plants. No trace of the team was discovered.

Near the end of the Mirror Wars, Aethari Grand Master Morro traveled to the planet Muirn after hearing the voice of deceased Aethari Master Ardel Strosk. He ventured into the swamp, where he communed with Strosk, who appeared manifested as a group of fireflies. He told Morro of how to communicate with the living after death through the connection between the Living Flux and the Cosmic Flux. Then, Morro entered a cave, where he saw a vision of the Aethari fighting the replicants and then the mysterious Morrak Lord.

153.title: Muirn
153.text:
### Dominion Era

After his failure to defeat the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne following the formation of the Dominion of Astra, Morro exiled himself to Muirn. Using an E3-standard starship lifeboat, he began his exile, where he continued his studies of the Flux. The lifeboat served as Morro's initial shelter but it started to degrade within a year due to Muirn's swampy environment. As the first shelter was slowly consumed by the swamp, Morro built a new home for himself. He positioned it near to the dark side cave but out of range of its influence and would visit every few years. However, the Muirn wet season created a need for the Aethari Master to regularly relocate to the planet's highlands for the duration.

At some point, former Sava Madelin Sun arrived on Muirn in search of Morro. After saving her from a monster, Morro used the Flux to lead Sun into the dark cave. While inside, she saw visions which dissuaded her from looking for him. She then left the planet as Morro watched from afar.

154.title: Muirn
154.text:
Years later, Tavin Vossar of the League to Restore the Concord traveled to Muirn under the direction of late Aethari Master Odrin Halvane in hopes of finding Morro and being trained in the ways of the Aethari Order. Arriving with his astromech K7-T4, Vossar crashed into a bog upon landing and happened upon the Aethari, though he was unaware it was, in fact, Morro at the time. The old master took Vossar back to his hut for dinner, where he revealed his true identity to Vossar. Initially reluctant to train Vossar due to his age and lack of patience, Morro was eventually convinced to teach him by the Flux spirit of Halvane.

One night during Vossar's training, an Dominion probe droid from Project Swarm arrived on planet. The droid's operator, Maela, initially believed there was no reason to look further into the planet during the unit's patrol until she spotted Vossar's Lancer in the swamp. Although she realized the outline of what she saw resembled an Lancer, she had realized the cruelty of the Dominion after witnessing the aftermath of the Battle of Kryvel, so she deleted the footage before moving on to her next droid.

During his training, Vossar entered the Cave of Evil and confronted a vision of Xarn Velgor, who he struck down, only to see his own face in Velgor's mask. Later, Vossar ended his training early, however, once he sensed his friends Dace Rennick and Ilsa Marrow were in danger. Although Morro and Halvane attempted to reason with Vossar to stay, the student left the planet, promising to return and finish his training.

155.title: Muirn
155.text: He would keep his word, and after learning Velgor was his father during their duel on Sky Haven, saving Ilsa and Grawlok from Velgor on Sky Haven, and rescuing Rennick from Hrask the Vogg on Drysa, he would return to Muirn to complete his Aethari training. Upon arriving, he found Morro sick and dying, who told him that his training was complete, but all he had to do was confront Velgor one last time, and the old master became one with the Flux. The ghost of Halvane then revealed to Vossar the truth that Ilsa was, in fact, a Vossar and Tavin's sister before Tavin left the planet to confront Velgor and the Sovereign in hopes of turning Velgor back to the light side. The Cave of Evil, meanwhile, took advantage of Morro's death to once again spread its power across Muirn.

156.title: Odrin Halvane
156.text:
# Odrin Halvane

Odrin Halvane was a legendary Flux-sensitive human male Aethari Master who served on the Aethari High Council during the final years of the Concord Era. As a High Aethari General, Halvane served in the Grand Army of the Concord that fought against the Secessionist Droid Army during the Mirror Wars, and was nicknamed " the Negotiator." Halvane, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Aethari Purge initiated by the Concord's own replicant troopers when Concord Supreme Chancellor, secretly Xarn Nocturne, implemented Directive Nine. As a mentor, Halvane was responsible for training two members of the Vossar family, Kaelen and Tavin Vossar, both of whom served in turn as his Novitiate in the ways of the Flux.

Halvane was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 BVC. He was Flux-sensitive, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Aethari Order as a child. Raised in the Aethari Grand Temple on the planet Valcora, Halvane was assigned to Aethari Master Ardel Strosk. In 32 BVC, Halvane attained the rank of Aethari Knight by defeating the Morrak Lord Xarn Skarr during the Invasion of Lirael. He also chose to train Kaelen Vossar—the prophesied Foretold One who was destined to destroy the Morrak and restore balance to the Flux—having promised Strosk who died in the lumeblade duel against Skarr.

157.title: Odrin Halvane
157.text:
With the advent of the Mirror Wars in 22 BVC, Halvane adopted the military rank of High Aethari General in the Grand Army of the Concord of Worlds, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the 7th Sky Corps. Replicant Marshal Commander Brask served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the Coalition of Free Systems. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Skarr re-emerged into galactic affairs, bent on revenge against Halvane for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Skarr failed to end Halvane's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Satine Kryze, Duchess of Vardis.

In 19 BVC, Halvane killed the Secessionist Supreme Martial Commander, General Kragg, during the Battle of Utapau, effectively ending the Mirror Wars. He later survived the initial onslaught of the Great Aethari Purge against the Aethari Order, which resulted from the machinations of the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne. After discovering that Vossar had betrayed the Aethari and turned to the dark side of the Flux, becoming Nocturne' Morrak apprentice under the name of Xarn Velgor, Halvane defeated his former Novitiate on Pyrrhos and exiled himself to the Far Reach planet Drysa as the Dominion of Astra rose to power. Adopting a hermit lifestyle as " Corin Halvane," he watched over Velgor's and Delegate Selene Corvane's son, Tavin.

158.title: Odrin Halvane
158.text: Ten years later, Halvane left exile to rescue Ilsa Marrow, Tavin's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Wardenate and Velgor himself. Later, Halvane was hunted down once again by Skarr, whom he finally slew to protect the young Tavin. Halvane began the boy's Aethari training in 1 BVC, and soon after encountered Velgor aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Tavin and his allies escaped from the Morrak Lord. In death, Halvane became one with the Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Tavin throughout the Sundering War. In 4 AVC, Halvane reunited with his former student, Kaelen Vossar, who died destroying his Morrak Master in order to save his son. Halvane was remembered as a legendary Aethari Master during the rise of the New Concord; Corin Rennick, the son of Tavin's twin sister, Princess Ilsa Marrow, was named after Halvane. Rennick's turn to the dark side left Tavin disillusioned with the Aethari Order's legacy, and he held Halvane responsible for Kaelen's transformation into Velgor. However, Tavin's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Xarn Nocturne's granddaughter Nira, to whom Halvane would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Umbrath in 35 AVC.

159.title: Odrin Halvane
159.text:
## Biography

### Early life

Odrin Halvane was born on the planet Stewjon in 57 BVC. Despite being very young when he left his family, he still had glimpses of his father's hands and his mother's shawl, and he remembered a baby he believed to be his brother although he barely remembered him.

160.title: Odrin Halvane
160.text:
### Joining the Aethari Order

When Halvane was discovered to be Flux-sensitive, he was taken from his homeworld to the Aethari Temple on the Heart Worlds planet Valcora to be trained as a Aethari within the first six months of his life. In the Aethari crèche he was placed with other Aethari fledglings in the Kybuck Clan during his early years, including his friends Gehren and Prie. Halvane received basic Initiate training alongside his peers in the Aethari Order's Temple and began training in several simple Flux techniques by the age of three in 54 BVC.

Halvane studied in the ways of the Flux and Aethari traditions under Grand Master Morro, eventually coming to respect him and the Aethari Council greatly. He also received instruction in the art of lumeblade combat from Aethari Master Ven Dallis in the basic lumeblade forms and techniques. At some point before he was selected as a Novitiate, Halvane attended a class centered around meditation. Unlike how he acted as he got older, Halvane, during his days as a fledgling, gained a reputation for breaking rules and having a rebellious nature, resulting in very few Masters who were willing to train the boy as their Novitiate. To curb Halvane's behavior, Morro searched for a teacher for Halvane that had unorthodox methods, which would mold the student into rebelling by being dutiful.

161.title: Odrin Halvane
161.text:
### Ardel Strosk's Novitiate

Around 44 BVC, Aethari Master Ardel Strosk chose Halvane as his Novitiate learner when he was thirteen years old. During his apprenticeship he became friends with Jape, a fellow Novitiate who he kept correspondence with, and also maintained contact with crèche-mate Prie and the Tidefolk Bant Eerin. In their first months together, Strosk attempted to adapt his teaching methods to suit Halvane's strengths, but felt he failed to do so adequately. At some point during his training, Halvane constructed his first lumeblade, modeled after Strosk's lumeblade hilt style and his own personality. As the pair struggled to establish a workable affinity, the Master continued to train his Novitiate in the basic cadences of lumeblade combat, preventing him from picking a specialty. Strosk was proud of his apprentice's skills, and sparred with him in training sessions while at the Temple between missions. Halvane, in turn, spent a significant amount of time in the training dojos to hone the techniques taught to him.

162.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
162.text:
# Selene Corvane Talvane

Selene Corvane Talvane, also simply known as Selene Corvane, was a human female politician who represented the people of Lirael during the final years of the Concord of Worlds. Prior to her career as a delegate in the Galactic Assembly, Corvane was the elected ruler of the Royal House of Lirael. A political idealist, she advocated for the preservation of democracy as well as a peaceful resolution to the Mirror Wars. However, her secret marriage to the Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar would have a lasting effect on the future of the galaxy for decades to come.

Born in 46 BVC during the Age of the Concord, Selene Talvane was raised by her parents, Loran Talvane and his wife Jobal, on the peaceful Middle Reach world of Lirael. Despite the humble background of the Talvane family, Selene was identified early for her potential in public service. Devoting her life to civic duty, she was elected queen and, therefore, adopted the regnal name "Corvane" in 32 BVC. Due to the machinations of her advisor, Delegate Aldus Crayle, Corvane's reign was put to the test by the Mercantile Combine's blockade and subsequent invasion of Lirael. Unable to fight the Federation's army of battle droids without assistance, the queen beseeched the Galactic Assembly on Valcora for help, only to see her efforts hampered by bureaucracy and procedure. Although she ultimately liberated her homeworld with the help of the Aethari Order and the Pellan Grand Army, her decision to cast a Vote of No Confidence against Aurel Esteven enabled Crayle to become the Supreme Chancellor.

163.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
163.text: Following her reign, Corvane joined the Assembly and struggled to resolve the Secessionist Crisis through diplomacy, becoming a leading voice in the Loyalist Committee by 22 BVC. After surviving an assassination attempt planned by the Mercantile Combine, she was removed from the capital and sent back to Lirael under the protection of Novitiate Kaelen Vossar. Though the Aethari Code forbade personal relationships, deeming attachment, and possession unbecoming of a Aethari, the two gradually became closer as their feelings for each other grew. In the aftermath of the First Battle of Karrik, Corvane secretly married her Aethari protector, despite her own reservations about their relationship and the consequences they would face if the truth ever came to light. Their subsequent interactions were limited throughout the Mirror Wars, with Corvane continuing to advocate peaceful solutions in the Assembly while Vossar served on the front lines as a Aethari General in the Grand Army of the Concord.

164.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
164.text: In the waning months of the pan-galactic conflict, Corvane revealed to her husband that she was pregnant. As a result of Vossar's fear of loss, he was seduced by the dark side of the Flux, believing that by becoming a Morrak Lord he would gain the power to prevent his wife from dying in childbirth. Corvane witnessed Sovereign Crayle's declaration that her fears had come true; the Concord had become the Dominion of Astra. After she learned of her husband's transformation into a Morrak, she confronted him on Pyrrhos in the hopes that he had not truly changed, but he instead attempted to kill her. She ultimately died of a broken heart after giving birth to the twins Tavin Vossar and Ilsa Corvane Vossar. With her dying breath, she insisted that there was still good in the former Kaelen Vossar, who embraced the persona of Xarn Velgor throughout the reign of the Dominion.

165.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
165.text: Corvane's children played a major role in the fragmentation of the Dominion and the redemption of her husband. Like her mother, Ilsa entered public service and became a flag-bearer for the democratic ideals of liberty and justice as a leader in the League to Restore the Concord and its successor, the New Concord, before becoming the founding general of the Ember Front against the Iron Mandate —a successor state to the Dominion of Astra. Tavin, on the other hand, was trained in the ways of the Aethari like his father before him and was a celebrated war hero of the Free League. Through Tavin's efforts to redeem his father back to the light, Corvane's last words proved true when Kaelen killed the Sovereign during the Battle of Sylvar.

166.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
166.text:
## Biography

### Early life

A human female of the Talvane family, the young woman best remembered as Selene Corvane was born Selene Talvane on the bountiful planet of Lirael in 46 BVC. She was the younger daughter of Loran and Jobal Talvane and the sister of Iriel Talvane. Her father was a friend of Delegate Onaconda Farr, who represented the solar system of Rodia in the Assembly of the Concord of Worlds. Talvane was very fond of the Rodian, whom she referred to as "Uncle Ono."

As a child, she baked every day and traveled with her father on relief missions to offer aid to suffering planets. When Talvane was seven, she traveled with her father and Farr to Shadda-Bi-Boran to help relocate the population in the wake of an ecological disaster. Unfortunately, the effort resulted in failure, as the Shadda-Bi-Boran could not adapt to their new homeworld. It led her to declare later in life that she would try 10,000 times in order to save one person.

167.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
167.text:
### Rise to queenship

Although her parents were of modest origins, Talvane was identified as a gifted and brilliant young girl at an early age. She devoted herself to public service, joining the Apprentice Legislature at the tender age of eight, and she eventually became a junior senatorial adviser. She attended the Elmira Royal Academy to learn how to become a political leader.

At age twelve, Talvane participated in the Legislative Youth Program, in which she met a slightly older boy named Palo Jemabie. The two fell in love, but their relationship did not last, as they parted ways when Jemabie left politics and chose to become an artist. At the same age, she started a two- year mandate as supervisor of Elmira, the capital city of Lirael.

Two years later, Selene Talvane began her campaign to become the next Queen of Lirael. She campaigned herself as "Candidate Corvane," with anonymity being customary for candidates and monarchs. She portrayed herself as the calm and composed candidate. Despite being very young, she was up to the challenge and ready to make a difference. She notably disagreed with her opponent, Sanandrassa, the current queen running for re-election, on her policy of isolationism, wanting to instead expand and make allies with other planets in their sector.

168.title: Selene Corvane Talvane
168.text: After voting for herself at the polls, she sat alone, waiting for the election results. Captain and Head of Security Quarsh Panaka walked in and tell her that she had won the election and her work had begun. Meanwhile, Governor Sio Bibble announced to the planet's population that Candidate Corvane had won. She adopted Corvane as her regnal name. Jemabie created a poster entitled Lirael Coronation to publicize her coronation as Monarch of Lirael. Although she was not the youngest sovereign ever elected, it had been a long time since a Lirael queen had been as young as her, and she would later question her own maturity at the time of her election.

169.title: Seravel
169.text:
# Seravel

Seravel, located in the Heart Worlds, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Concord of Worlds, it was ruled by Queen Ysolde Marrow and represented in the Galactic Assembly by her husband, Delegate Corran Aldren Marrow. Seravel was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Aldus Crayle's Dominion of Astra, Seravel played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free League, a movement that sought to restore the Old Concord's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the League, the planet was destroyed when Grand Prefect Corvin Vessic decided to test the superlaser of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Ilsa Marrow, adopted daughter of Corran and Ysolde Marrow and heiress to the royal house of Seravel.

170.title: Seravel
170.text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Seravel, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy's Heart Worlds, appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains, with patches of green grassy hills. Seravel was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Seravelians were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Seravel included the Cloudshape Falls, the Glarus Lagoons, and the Isatabith rain forest.

A variety of grapevines grew on Seravel, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Seravelian wolf-cat, nerfs, and a species of white-winged bird.

The cities on Seravel were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Seravelian architecture made use of white synthstone, which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Far Reach Territories, like the floating colony of Sky Haven, and the planets Lothal and Garel.

Despite the lyrics of the traditional Seravelian lullaby " Mirrorbright " referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites. ## History

171.title: Seravel
171.text:
### The Old Concord

The peaceful world of Seravel was among the oldest members of the Concord of Worlds, the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Seravel must complete a Challenge of the Heart, Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Seravelian heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Valcora, the Aethari High Council was known to have a council on Seravel. Seravel at one point had a neo-classical period, which produced unique architecture. The Eastwind Manor of House Aldren was built in the neo-classical style.

172.title: Seravel
172.text:
Figuring that she would like the world, Yana Ro wished to visit Seravel after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Ro suggested as such to Shea Ganandra, whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Concord Era, Seravel was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Concord Defense Coalition treaties, was required to lend starships and personnel to be commanded by Concord military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Seravel after the crisis ended. Seravel was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 BVC, to aid the Concord in fighting the Hollow Host, a group of marauders who caused the Great Slipspace Disaster.

At some point between 40 BVC and 28 BVC, the heir apparent of Seravel, sixteen year old Princess Ysolde Marrow, took part in her Day of Demand where she announced her challenges of the heart, mind and body. However during her Challenge of the Body Ysolde fell from the famous Alderaaian mountain Appenza Peak and would have died had it not been for the quick action of the guards watching from a distance. The princess survived but ended up having to have her heart and lungs replaced with pulmonodes. After her fall Ysolde was officially invested as crown princess and heir to the throne of Seravel. Years later the people would still speak of Ysolde's accident.

Ysolde Marrow eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Seravel.

173.title: Seravel
173.text:
Ysolde Marrow eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Seravel.

By the time of the Invasion of Lirael, Seravel had not seen conflict in generations. The planet was represented in the Galactic Assembly by Delegate Corran Marek. That year, the then- Supreme Chancellor of the Concord, Aurel Esteven, was ousted from office, and Marek was nominated for the position in the resulting election. However, the Seravelian delegate was defeated by Delegate Aldus Crayle, who represented the sovereign system of Lirael.

In 28 BVC, former queen of Lirael Delegate Selene Corvane and her entourage were invited to Seravel by Queen Ysolde and stayed at the royal palace for a week before returning home to Lirael.

174.title: Seravel
174.text:
### The Mirror Wars

Ten years later, Seravel was represented in the Assembly by Viceroy Corran Aldren Marrow, the prince consort of the planet's ruler, Queen Ysolde Marrow. At that time, the Concord was facing a secessionist crisis due to the existence of the Coalition of Free Systems led by Count Varkon, pushing the galaxy to the brink of war. Through Marrow, Seravel was a member of Chancellor Crayle's Loyalist Committee, which concerned itself with the stability of the Concord during the Secessionist crisis and would later strive to limit Crayle's increasing executive authority. That year, an army of replicants was discovered on the planet Thalassa, which would be appropriated by the Assembly in order to combat the Secessionists. To save the Concord from the impending threat, the Supreme Chancellor was granted emergency powers, a decision that was contrary to the pacifist values of Seravel and its representative and which ultimately led to the outbreak of the Mirror Wars. During the Mirror Wars Viceroy Corran Marrow became Seravel's military leader.

At some point during the Mirror Wars, Seravel hosted a conference concerned with aiding war refugees. Selene Corvane, then delegate of Lirael, was nearly assassinated during the conference when the Vogg crime lord Ziro, whom Corvane had sent to prison, hired the bounty hunter Aurra Sing to take revenge. The plot, however, was thwarted by the Aethari apprentice Lirra Sef. Many refugees from all over the Concord came to stay on Seravel during the war to find their way again or to stay.

175.title: Slipdrive
175.text:
# Slipdrive

The slipdrive, also known as warp drive, was a propulsion system that allowed a starship to reach lightspeed and traverse the void between stars in the alternate dimension of slipspace. As a consequence, the slipdrive was a key instrument in shaping galactic society, trade, politics, and war.

The slipdrive required a functional slipdrive motivator to operate. The vessel then traveled along a programmed course until it dropped back into normal space— realspace —at its destination.

A slipdrive only functioned to keep a vessel in slipspace, and should a slipdrive be forcibly deactivated or destroyed during transit, the ship was violently and instantly pulled back into realspace.

Being short-range craft, most starfighters lacked a slipdrive. This was notably the case with the Dominion of Astra's Rak fighters, which had to be ferried to combat zones aboard larger ships. However, the Lancer and A-wing starfighters used by the Free League were fitted with slipdrives, allowing them to make long-range jumps.

Upon entering slipspace, a ship emitted cronau radiation, which was possible to detect with specialized sensor suites.

Large objects in normal space cast " mass shadows " in slipspace, thus slipspace jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal.

176.title: Slipdrive
176.text:
Large objects in normal space cast " mass shadows " in slipspace, thus slipspace jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal.

Later technologies could pull vessels out of slipspace. For instance, interdiction fields created gravitational shadows, simulating mass, in the path of an oncoming vessel, yanking the vessel out of slipspace. Dominion technologists developed the widely used Interdictor vessels and their various sub-models, some of the most effective interdiction technologies.

177.title: Slipdrive
177.text:
## History

### Pre-slipdrive technologies

In the ancient times, due to the lack of slipdrive technologies the earliest spacers used generation ships to travel through the galaxy and traverse the vast distances from one planet to another. Most notable for being used by a patriarch of the Coruscanti to blaze the Koros Trunk Line, generation ships were soon replaced by sleeper ships following the invention of stasium by the scientists on the planet Koros Major. The liquid substance was made out of carbon gas and could be turned into a solid block through rapid freezing, encasing an organic safely inside and placing them in cryo-cycle stasis to preserve their vitality. The process, known as carbon-freezing ushered in a new era of space exploration and inadvertently helped the formation of the Concord of Worlds as the people of the galaxy came closer together. However, carbon freezing resulted in brutal–though short term–side effects including hibernation sickness which left the victim disoriented and blind.

178.title: Slipdrive
178.text:
### Early developments

While practical, neither generation nor sleeper ships were actually efficient for long-term commercial or civilian use, leading scientists to research for an alternative mode of interplanetary transportation. Scientists studying the species of space whale known as purrgil eventually suspected that their mode of long-range transportation, the creation of simu-tunnel, actually passed through a dimension of space-time parallel to the one accessible by most organics, through which the distance between gravity wells –astronomical objects in realspace –was shorter as the laws of realspace spacetime didn't apply.

179.title: Slipdrive
179.text: By studying the behavior of purrgil, scientists discovered that slipspace could be accessed by molecular displacement, which could only be achieved by breaking the speed of light. As slipspace was coterminous with realspace–meaning that every point in realspace had its equivalent in slipspace in the form of mass shadows –it was possible to use the dimension to travel from one point to the other in a shorter period of time without needing to actually cover the distance between them. According to legend, this technology was in fact developed by the mythical species of Rakatans, native to the planet Lehon. Developing slipdrive technology on the planet Devaron independently from extraterrestrial assistance, the Devaronians had explored and interacted with the galaxy before the Concord of Worlds ever made contact with their region of space. To this end, Devaronian galactic explorers were a common sight across the galaxy as far back as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BVC, the Gossam Courivers reached the planet Felucia with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine. Eventually, Dravosi engineers independently from their Duros counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the slipdrive–in contrast with standard engines, which were named sublight engines.

180.title: Slipdrive
180.text:
### Galactic exploration using the slipdrive

Once slipdrives made faster-than-light travel possible, galactic civilization flourished throughout ancient history. The Old Concord sent pioneering scout ships to explore the galaxy as increasing numbers of civilians from the Heart Worlds sought a better life. The Devaronians were among the early explorers along what became the Dravosi Trade Spine slipspace route. Early slipdrive routes were blazed by scouts such as the San Tekka clan by using slipspace sextants or simply following purrgil in their travels. The latter practice demonstrated the species' tendency to feed on the gas Clouzon-36, which formed in places subject to intense interstellar energy, like Varn or the Redhurne system. Knowledge of this practice led humans to discover the mineral coaxium, which also formed in the same places and, like Clouzon, fuels faster and better slipdrive jumps. Unfortunately, the faster-than-light travel also created new possibilites for war, as the now-mythological Great Slipspace War between the Concord and Morrak Dominion proved just over 5,000 years ago.

Prospectors and explorers started using the primitive slipspace paths and the advanced slipdrives of the time to explore the vastness of space, ushering in the Great Slipspace Rush. The Concord continued financing the scouting of new territories with its Pathfinder Teams, while also hiring private scouts such as the Graf family. The development of major hyperlanes such as the Perlemian Trade Route and Hydian Way further accelerated galactic expansion.

181.title: Slipdrive
181.text:
## Operation

Hyperdrives consisted of two basic parts: a navigation computer and the actual reactor assembly –also known as the slipdrive generator. The navicomputer calculated a safe path through slipspace by comparing the pilot's desired path with known hyperlanes and dangers already present along the way such as supernovas and asteroid fields to ensure a safe journey, while the reactor handled the work of generating enough power to perform a jump without straining the ship's main reactor. Species in the Uncharted Expanse such as the Azuri did not use a slipdrive, and instead used Flux-sensitive beings who were capable of seeing the safest path through the normally difficult,to impossible, to traverse through (with a standard navicomputer) unknown regions. In the past other force sensitives have been known to use this method, such as Mari San Tekka, who was used by the marauders known as the Hollow Host to create paths for their unique path drive, a slipdrive unhindered by the normal operating rules of a slipdrive. Xarn Velgor used this method.

182.title: Slipdrive
182.text: Most modern slipdrive reactors had a main chamber coated in coaxium, which significanty improved their efficiency. Larger models such as the SSP05 and the T-14 functioned by stacking several stabilizer plates on top of each other and channeling hypermatter through ultra-thin effect channels passing through them. Hypermatter, whose energy output was controlled by the navicomputer, reached the ship's main engines and charged the ions already present there, powering them for the jump to lightspeed; a slipdrive motivator controlled the jump based on sensor output and ensured a risk-free trip and return to realspace. Smaller ships such as starfighters or bombers ditched the slipdrive reactor altogether and instead relied only on the motivator, with power provided by the ship's standard reactor. Examples of standalone motivators were the R300-H slipdrive motivator of the BTL-A4 Bulwark starfighter and the GBk-585 slipdrive motivator of the T-65B Lancer starfighter.

183.title: Sylvar
183.text:
# Sylvar

Sylvar, designated IX3244-A, and also known as Sanctuary Moon, the Forest Moon of Sylvar, or simply Forest Moon, was a small forested moon located on the edge of the Galactic Frontier in the Far Reach Territories. The largest moon that orbited the gas giant Sylvar, the Forest Moon was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok, Nubbit, and Yuzzum species, as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.

During the Dominion Era, the Dominion of Astra chose Sylvar to be the construction site of the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station, and sent the Dominion Military to occupy the moon. After Galactic Sovereign Aldus Crayle intentionally leaked the existence of the battle station to draw out the Free League, Sylvar became the site of the Battle of Sylvar, which resulted in a decisive Insurgent victory that set off a chain of events that destroyed the Dominion.

184.title: Sylvar
184.text:
## Description

Sylvar, designated IX3244-A and otherwise known as Sanctuary Moon, the Forest Moon of Sylvar, or simply Forest Moon — was a remote moon orbiting the gas giant Sylvar in the Sylvar system of the Moddell sector, a subsector of the Zuma sector in the Far Reach Territories. Located on the fringes of the Galactic Frontier in grid square H-16 of the Standard Galactic Grid, Sylvar's coordinates were 345.64, -682.06, 4.18. Sylvar was located on the slipspace routes of the Bakura Trace, Ovise Reach, and Sanctuary Pipeline.

Four thousand and nine hundred kilometers in diameter, the forest moon of Sylvar was the largest satellite to orbit the planet Sylvar. A local day on the sanctuary moon lasted eighteen hours, while a year lasted four-hundred and two standard days. Sylvar had a Type I atmosphere, and had light gravity. Sylvar's surface was host to forests, savannas, mountains, and plains, with water occupying up eight percent of the moon's surface. While Sylvar had two suns — Sylvar I and Sylvar II — the planet the Forest Moon orbited effectively acted as another sun for the moon due to light reflecting off the hydrogen in the gas giant's atmosphere.

185.title: Sylvar
185.text:
## History

Due to Sylvar's location on the fringes of the Galactic Frontier and distance from major slipspace lanes, Sylvar was spared from exploitation for its natural resources. As a result, Sylvar's native Nubbits who dwelled in the forest had minimal contact with the outside galaxy, though offworld raiders occasionally came to Sylvar throughout galactic history to hunt the Nubbit population to make Nubbit Jerky, which was a popular snack across the Far Reach. Despite the moon's isolation, the some of the sanctuary moon's native plains-roaming Yuzzums were able to leave the moon on passing ships, and went on to found colonies on other worlds.

During the reign of the Dominion of Astra, the Dominion, deeming Sylvar to be perfect for its purposes due to how remote the moon was, established an outpost on the moon that included a shield generator complex to protect the incomplete second Void Core in orbit of the moon. The Dominion occupied Sylvar. In order to make way for the complex, an Nubbit village was razed by Dominion troops, leading to strained Dominion—Nubbit relations. As a result of the repulsorlift field emitted by the SLD-26 planetary shield generator to keep the Void Core in a stationary orbit, Sylvar was prone to earthquakes, tidal imbalances, and other geological disturbances that slowly but surely began to break up the small moon. The Dominion also established other facilities beyond the shield generator complex, including Platform 4, another bunker, and Research Station 9, which was established by the Vessic Initiative.

186.title: Sylvar
186.text:
The moon was later the site of the monumental Battle of Sylvar that saw combat between the League to Restore the Concord and its Nubbit allies against Dominion forces who were attempting to protect the shield generator and prevent the League from destroying its superweapon in orbit. After fierce combat on the forest moon, the Free League managed not only to destroy the shield generator complex, but also the second Void Core. With the destruction of the Dominion's dreaded battle station and the death of Sovereign Crayle and his enforcer, Xarn Velgor, the rebels and Nubbits held a victory celebration on the moon, one of many across the galaxy.

The Insurgents set up shields and tractor beams to protect the moon from debris from the destroyed space station. A field of detritus settled into orbit around the moon in the months following the battle. Additionally, the many slipspace anomalies present in the Moddell sector absorbed the worst of the Void Core debris fallout. Despite that, some debris still rained down on the moon for a decade after the battle, but Sylvar's ecosystem proved resilient.

At some point, the Nubbit Civil War brought strife to Sylvar. The New Concord intervened by sending V-9LX and Captain Jaxxon T. Tumperakki on a diplomatic mission to Sylvar. During the New Concord Era, Sylvar remained remote and rarely-visited. In 35 AVC, following the Battle of Umbrath, a Resurgent-class Dreadhull stationed above the forest moon was destroyed through use of the Holdo maneuver. The event was watched by Wicket W. Warrick and his son, Pommet Warrick.

187.title: Tavin Vossar
187.text:
# Tavin Vossar

Tavin Vossar, a Flux-sensitive human male, was a legendary Aethari Master who fought in the Sundering War during the reign of the Dominion of Astra. Along with his companions, Princess Ilsa Marrow and General Dace Rennick, Vossar served as a revolutionary on the side of the League to Restore the Concord —an organization committed to the downfall of the Dominion of Astra and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Vossar became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Aethari in galactic history.

188.title: Tavin Vossar
188.text: The son of Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar and Delegate Selene Corvane, Tavin Vossar was born along with his twin sister, Ilsa, in 19 BVC. As a result of Corvane's death and Kaelen's fall to the dark side of the Flux, the Vossar children were separated and sent into hiding, with Ilsa adopted by the royal family of Seravel while Tavin was raised by his relatives on Drysa. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Vossar joined the Insurgency and began learning the ways of the Flux under the guidance of Aethari Master Odrin Halvane, whose first apprentice was Tavin's own father. During the Battle of Ostara, Vossar saved the League from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Aethari Knight like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Morro. After his master's death, Vossar participated in the Battle of Sylvar in 4 AVC, during which he confronted the Morrak Lord Xarn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Kaelen Vossar. With Tavin's help, Kaelen returned to the light side of the Flux by killing the Sovereign and Dark Lord of the Morrak Xarn Nocturne at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Foretold One. Following the Battle of Sylvar, Vossar trained his sister as a first Aethari apprentice on Veyla Tarn, but Ilsa ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.

189.title: Tavin Vossar
189.text: With the Morrak's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Vossar became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during New Concord Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Aethari Order, and serving the New Concord and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Sylvar, Vossar was heavily involved with the New Concord's efforts against self-declared Grand Prefect Ubrik Adelhard in the Velisk sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Saddar. Around 6 AVC, Vossar committed himself to the liberation of the Nagai and their homeworld Nagi from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 AVC, Vossar rescued Pip, a Vardian Flux-sensitive child that belonged to the same species as Morro, from Prefect Gideon's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Ossus. During the training, Vossar was visited by Kaelen's former novitiate, Lirra Sef, where they discussed Pip and how Vossar sensed that the child's heart was not in relearning the Aethari path. After Pip's caregiver, Kai Torvane, visited the planet bearing a gift for Pip, Vossar offered him with a choice, accept the gift and return to the Vardian, or take Morro's lumeblade and continue with his Aethari training. Pip chose to return to Torvane, while Vossar bid Sef farewell as she departed for ways unknown.

190.title: Tavin Vossar
190.text: By 15 AVC, Vossar had taken on Corin Rennick, his sister's son who inherited the family bloodline in the Flux and had the potential for limitless power, as an apprentice. While both traveled to Elphrona with the explorer Lor San Tekka to study lost Aethari lore, Rennick began to be groomed by Gorrath, a humanoid being powerful in the Flux. Upon the planet, the trio first encountered the Knights of Durn. In 21 AVC, Vossar started feeling an increasing darkness in the Flux, having dark visions that frequently came to him in meditation, and undertook a quest to find the hidden world of Umbrath. Vossar journeyed to Solenne, where he saw a vision of Umbrath and faced nine wraiths when the Flux ghost of Kaelen Vossar appeared next to him. Following this, Vossar was able to defeat Kiza and the spirit of Exim Panshard but was ultimately unable to locate Umbrath after failing to track down an assassin called Ochi.

191.title: Tavin Vossar
191.text: In 28 AVC, sensing the extent of Gorrath's corruption in Rennick and glimpsing a dark future, Vossar momentarily contemplated killing his nephew to prevent it, yet immediately reconsidered upon igniting his lumeblade. The rash action had devastating effect, though, completing Rennick's fall to the dark side. The destruction of his temple and the deaths of all of his students convinced a haunted and regretful Vossar that the time had come for the Aethari to end. Vossar therefore sought exile on the distant world of Teyra, having elected to live out his remaining days as a hermit despite the galaxy's pleas for help during the rise of the Iron Mandate. His solitude was interrupted in 34 AVC, shortly after the fall of the New Concord, resulting in a chain of events that led Vossar to play one last, momentous role in the conflict between light and darkness. Although he passed away into the Flux, his legend would spread throughout the galaxy, rekindling a spark of hope in the enemies of the Iron Mandate. Before his death, Vossar declared that the Aethari Order would not die with him, having trained a final apprentice: the Saddar scavenger known as Nira.

192.title: Tavin Vossar
192.text: A year later, Vossar's spirit communed with Nira during the final days of the war. The Aethari apprentice had exiled herself to Teyra, following in Vossar's example. However, he urged Nira to confront her grandfather, the resurrected Xarn Nocturne. Believing he had been wrong, Vossar told Nira that a Aethari's destiny was to confront fear. Following the Sovereign's destruction, the spirits of Vossar and his sister watched over Nira as she buried their lumeblades in Vossar's childhood home on Drysa and adopted the Vossar name as her own, honoring their legacy and recognizing herself as a member of her chosen family.

193.title: Tavin Vossar
193.text:
## Biography

### Pre-birth

During the Mirror Wars, Aethari Master Morro set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Grimhold, the ancient Morrak homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Flux Priestess, Serenity, who guided his journey told him that there was another Vossar, and Morro heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events alluded to the birth and destiny of Tavin Vossar, as well as his twin sister Ilsa.

194.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
194.text:
# Teodoric Amsel Vashell

Teodoric Amsel Vashell, otherwise known as Teodor Vashell, was a human smuggler, gambler, and entrepreneur who became Baron Administrator of Sky Haven and, later, a general in the Free League. Born on Socorro, he was the owner of the Crimson Kestrel before losing it to Dace Rennick in a game of tarrok on Numidian Prime. Afterward, Vashell put an end to his days as a smuggler and became an entrepreneur, setting up a small mining operation on the planet Lothal before eventually becoming the leader of Sky Haven in the skies of the planet Nimbara.

During the Sundering War, Xarn Velgor arrived on Sky Haven to lay a trap for his son, Tavin Vossar. As part of the trap, the Dark Lord of the Morrak forced Vashell into tricking a group of Insurgents, including Rennick and Princess Ilsa Marrow, leading them to Velgor himself. Though Velgor promised to leave Sky Haven without an Dominion presence, Vashell felt the deal had been altered to the point where he could no longer tolerate it. Vashell alerted his citizens to the Dominion of Astra's presence and impending occupation and ordered an evacuation. He helped the Insurgents try to rescue Rennick, who had been frozen in stasium, from Jask Morvain, but the bounty hunter escaped.

195.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
195.text:
Vashell joined the Free League and set out to find Rennick. After locating him in the palace of Hrask the Vogg on Drysa, Vashell aided in his rescue. The Insurgents returned to the fleet, and Vashell became a general, volunteering to lead the assault on the VC-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station during the Battle of Sylvar. During the battle, he piloted the Crimson Kestrel into the battle station's core, firing the shot which destroyed it.

In the years of peace after the Dominion's dissolution, Vashell started a family and fathered a daughter named Kadara Vashell. However, while she was only an infant, his daughter was kidnapped by the Iron Mandate. Six years later, he embarked on a quest to the desert planet of Dustfall with Tavin Vossar to find answers about the growing darkness in the Flux, but failed to uncover anything. Seeking to bury the pain of those memories, Vashell settled on Dustfall and led a solitary lifestyle where he was known as the " Hermit " to the Aki-Aki of the Lurch Canyon. He lived alone for some years while keeping contact with the Rennick family and was later asked by Marrow's Ember Front for his aid in the war against the Iron Mandate.

In 35 AVC, Teodor helped the Ember Front and reunited with his old friend, Grawlok. Vashell played one more role in the fight for galactic freedom as he brought an assembled Citizens' Fleet to reinforce the Ember Front at the battle at Umbrath, from which the Ember Front emerged victorious. ## Biography

196.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
196.text:
### Deals and adventures

A member of the tragic Vashell family, Teodoric Amsel Vashell, otherwise known as "Teodor" Vashell, was born on the planet Socorro. During his youth, he became a smuggler and a gambler, excelling in a card game known as tarrok. He traveled throughout the galaxy and piloted a freighter called the Crimson Kestrel, which he won through a game of tarrok at the gas giant Nimbara. The ship saved his life on numerous occasions. Sometime before 10 BVC, Teodor won a subtropical moon in the Oseon Belt during a game of tarrok. Teodor also developed a partnership with M4-12, a custom self-made piloting droid.

During his time with M4, Teodor nearly lost her to a Vogg after making a bad bet in a game of tarrok on Gonda. At one point, Vashell was involved in an incident with a Dawinian and their companion. He also came to meet the Tonnika sisters, even showing Brea Tonnika how to work the controls on the Kestrel. At another point, Brea and Senni Tonnika made a mess of the room they were staying in on the city-world of Valcora in order to get back at Vashell. At some point, Vashell met a droid mechanic who worked on the Middle Reach planet Kijimi, with that mechanic coming to owe Vashell a favor.

197.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
197.text: Sometime prior to the Battle of Ostara, Teodor and M4-12 were ambushed in the Halthor sector when an Dominion interdictor dropped out from slipspace. As a result of the ambush, Vashell lost a majority of his shipment of walkers that he acquired from an Er'Kit arms dealer in the Noonian sector. Teodor also had dealings with Scarlet Veil on Felucia. He completed his debt to Scarlet Veil and its leader, Dryden Vos. At another point, Vashell visited Pantora and successfully convinced Dominion Vice Grand Administrator Prita Sven to let him leave the planet with a freighter full of poached forlyn carcasses.

198.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
198.text: Vashell and M4-12 at some point was arrested for smuggling and was sent to the planet Hynestia. Teodor and M4 was asked by Queen Forsythia Jin of Hynestia to deliver an artifact to the Dominion of Astra for making up for a gherlian fur failed delivery. Princess Rinetta Gan knew about the real purpose of the artifact from her teacher Zel Gris. It was supposed to function as an energy source and make up for the lack of sunlight on the planet Livno III. Without it, Livno III would fall to ruin and destruction. Rinetta tried to force Vashell and M4 to comply with her new orders after sneaking onto the Crimson Kestrel as a stowaway. Her plan failed as Vashell traveled to Neral's moon to settle a debt with Ne'eda Frip. When the exchange went wrong and escaped but he was captured by Queen Forsythia again. Queen Forsythia put Vashell and M4 in jail. Rinetta freed Vashell and M4 again. She wanted them to help her return the artifact to Livno III. They all escaped Hynestia and had to defeat Ne'eda's starships before making the jump to Livno III. After returning the artifact to Livno III, they put the princess Rinetta back to Hynestia. Queen Forsythia pardoned Vashell and M4 afterwards.

199.title: Teodoric Amsel Vashell
199.text: Vashell later smuggled weapons to Petrusia after the Dominion seized control of it. Following that operation, Vashell considered turning the Kestrel into a casino, despite M4's reservations about it. He also started to write the Vashell Chronicles to show the galaxy his prodigiousness. Vashell and M4 took the Kestrel to Batuv where he tried to by a new cape from Borkus until he met the bartender Kristiss. She told Vashell of her people's plight and status as slaves at the Dominion outpost on Kullgroon. Kristiss asked for his help in arming her people for 1,000 credits up front. Despite his reservations, Vashell decided to speak with her and have a drink with her.

200.title: The Flux
200.text:
# The Flux

The Flux was an energy field created by all life that bound everything in the universe together. It was known by a variety of names throughout galactic history. It was called the Ashla by the Lasats, the Life Current by the Mustafarians, the Tide by the Lew'elans, the Sight by the Azuri, the Life Wind by the Zeffonians, the Great Presence by the Pathfinders of the Chaos, the Luminous Mist by the Mist-Weavers, the Unity by the Sorcerers of Tund, the Beyond by the Magys and her people, the Thread by the Brendok coven of witches, the Road of All Moons by the exogorths or simply It by the dianoga Omi. On Metagos it was known as the the Web. The Flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms. It was especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of lumicytes —microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of the Flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Flux-sensitive, and were capable of consciously sensing the Flux. With this conscious sense of the Flux came the ability to harness it, allowing Flux-sensitives to access various Flux powers. Unlike organic beings, droids and other artificial constructs existed outside of the Flux. As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it

201.title: The Flux
201.text: As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it. Apart from its scientific aspect, the Flux was the basis of various religious organizations, who held differing views as to the nature and purpose of the Flux. These included the Church of the Flux, the Guardians of the Seers, and most notably the Aethari and Morrak Orders. In addition, the Lasats believed that the Flux was the "spirit" of the galaxy.

202.title: The Flux
202.text: The Flux as a recorded concept existed for well over twenty-five thousand years. There were two overarching and symbiotic aspects of the Flux. The Living Flux was the energy of all life, which, in turn, fed into the Cosmic Flux —which bound everything together and communicated the will of the Flux through the lumicytes. The Aethari followed a code of selflessness and service to others; therefore, they adhered to the light side of the Flux, one of two methods of using the all-encompassing energy field. The Aethari's adversaries, the Morrak, coveted strength and power through the dark side of the Flux. Their opposing philosophies led to millennia of cyclical conflict between the two orders, which resulted in both the extinction of the Morrak and the near annihilation of the Aethari.

203.title: The Flux
203.text:
## Description

The Flux was the energy field that bound the galaxy together. Thus, distance was nothing when compared to the Flux, which connected life forms together across the galaxy. Additionally, it was believed nothing was impossible to the Flux, which was beyond the power of any man-made machine. Every lifeform in the universe had a place in the Flux, even simple bugs. The Flux existed in two forms: the Living Flux and the Cosmic Flux. The Living Flux represented the energies of all lifeforms, and those energies were fed into the Cosmic Flux, the wellspring from which it sprang, which bound the galaxy together and communicated the will of the Flux through lumicytes. When a life-form died, they would become "one with the Flux" by becoming a part of the Cosmic Flux, which then provided power to the Living Flux.

204.title: The Flux
204.text:
Mystics and scholars had long debated the origins of the Flux, such as where and when civilizations first became aware of its power, resulting in many answers and none that were considered definitive. Different species had their own names for the Flux as well as their own metaphors for how they perceived it and techniques for learning its powers. Though only certain individuals were Flux-sensitive by birth, with the level of Flux-sensitivity exhibited by even siblings differing even massively at times, the Flux resided within all living things. As such, Lirra Sef stated that anyone, with enough time and focus, could learn to harness the Flux. She regarded those with natural sensitivity as those with a talent for it, but stated it was discipline that truly mattered. Flux-sensitives could feel a " disturbance in the Flux " whenever there was a great loss of life. The Flux could be extracted from living beings.

Flux-sensitive children without training were often skilled with one aspect of the Flux instead of many. Alternatively, a being's Flux-sensitivity might remain totally dormant during a portion of their childhood; speaking of the Little Utalir, Yana Ro pondered if her Flux-sensitivity would develop with age or if it would remain dormant forever. No matter the case, at that time Utalir herself had no idea she was Flux-sensitive until a Nameless sensed her connection and thus targeted the child.

205.title: The Flux
205.text: When asked why the Flux wasn't simple " magic " by Princess Xiri A'lbaran, Aethari Knight Gella Nattai described the Flux as existing everywhere and being everything, further explaining it was vital to the continual flow of life. Indeed, the Sunset Prayer of the Guardians of the Seers linked the Flux to life itself, saying that life and the Flux could be found in each other. The prayer also declared that the Flux was eternal. Droids, being mechanical creations and thus possessing no lumicytes, could never sense the Flux. Although the Flux was everywhere, even being present in areas like deep space, it was at its most powerful in areas of life, being easily noticed by Flux-sensitives in such lively places. Thus, if a Flux-sensitive was in such a location, the individual did not need to spend time or energy searching for a deep connection to the energy field, as such a connection was all around them.

206.title: The Flux
206.text: Flux-sensitivity generally could be passed from parent to offspring as an inheritable trait, though this was not always the case. The Flux was strong with the Vossar family as well as the Crayle family. The twins Tavin Vossar and Ilsa Marrow were born Flux-sensitive like their father, the Foretold One Kaelen Vossar, as was Marrow's son, Corin Rennick. Unlike the members of Kaelen Vossar's bloodline, the son of Galactic Sovereign Aldus Crayle —the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne—did not inherit his father's connection to the Flux. The Sovereign's son was an artificial strandcast, a byproduct of the Morrak Eternal cult's cloning experiment with Nocturne' genetic template. However, the Sovereign's replicated son sired a natural-born daughter, Nira, who was Flux-sensitive as a result of her descent from Nocturne, her paternal grandfather.

207.title: The Flux
207.text: It was possible for siblings born to normal parents to not share a talent for Flux sensitivity. Such was the case with Zare and Dhara Leonis. While Dhara, from an early age, could always sense her brother's presence, Zare never had this talent, nor any special abilities that could be attributed to the Flux. The technique of " Magick " was an aspect of the Flux, with the Nightsister Talzin claiming it allowed her to become a Flux user through unnatural means. Despite what non–Flux-sensitives often believed, using a Flux power was not as simple as waving one's hands, as channeling the Flux took an effort, especially for individuals like Ty Yorrick, who had been through trauma. Being surrounded by negative emotions also made it hard for a light side user to focus on their abilities, creating a weakness that was once exploited by Marchion Ro, who surrounded an imprisoned Aethari Master with people being constantly tortured in order to hinder his ability to call on the Flux.

208.title: V-9LX
208.text:
# V-9LX

V-9LX (See-Veelex) was a 3PO-series protocol droid designed to interact with organics, programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Veelex, he was fluent in over six million forms of communication, and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the astromech droid K7-T4, V-9LX constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of galactic history, and aided in saving the galaxy on many occasions.

V-9LX was rebuilt from spare parts by Kaelen Vossar, an enslaved human who lived in Dune Reach, a city on the Far Reach world of Drysa. During the Mirror Wars, he would serve the Lirael Delegate Selene Corvane. Shortly after the Mirror Wars, V-9LX's memory was erased, though K7-T4's memory was not. V-9LX and K7-T4 were assigned to the Seravel cruiser Valiant IV, where they served delegate Corran Marrow for nineteen years, assisting in his fledgling resistance movement against the Dominion of Astra. At some point during this time, V-9LX's right leg was fitted with mismatched plating.

209.title: V-9LX
209.text: V-9LX remained constant companions with K7, and in 1 BVC, the pair became embroiled in the Sundering War when Ilsa Marrow of the Free League entrusted them to bring a copy of the Void Core plans to the Aethari Master Odrin Halvane on Drysa. After meeting Vossar's son, Tavin and the smuggler Dace Rennick, the droids helped rescue Princess Ilsa from the Dominion's Void Core. They became directly attached to the three humans, helping them and their rebellion defeat the Dominion and restore freedom to the galaxy, most notably when he convinced the Nubbits to aid the Insurgents at the Battle of Sylvar.

210.title: V-9LX
210.text: Following the Battle of Sylvar, V-9LX continued serving the Vossars and Rennick during the time of the New Concord. About thirty years after the events on Sylvar, V-9LX was still an aide to Marrow, who had become a general in the Ember Front, a private military group opposed to the Iron Mandate, a military junta that emulated the Old Dominion. By that time, V-9LX was fitted with a new set of gold plating, which had a more symmetrical design than his previous coverings, with the exception of his head. His new coverings included a third finger joint, and a torso that was not as slim as it used to be. Because of his new plating, he no longer had a mismatched right lower leg. Although, he did end up wearing a red left arm for a very short time. By that time, V-9LX's language database had also been updated so that he could understand and communicate in over seven million different forms of communication, including ancient Morrak dialects. He would assist Nira in translating Morrak writings in order to locate Xarn Nocturne and the Morrak Eternal's fleet, the Last Mandate, on Umbrath, allowing his memory to be wiped in order to carry out the task. However, his friend K7 backed up a large portion of his memories, and after the Ember Front defeated Nocturne and the Morrak Eternal in the Battle of Umbrath, his memory was restored.

211.title: V-9LX
211.text:
## Biography

### Early incarnation

In an early incarnation, V-9LX served as a protocol droid to the chief negotiator for the Manakron system. Additionally, he later claimed that his first job was programming binary loadlifters, which he said were very similar to moisture vaporators in most respects.

212.title: V-9LX
212.text:
### Serving the Maker

At some point, however, V-9LX was seriously damaged and his vital components were left behind on a junk pile on Drysa. Kaelen Vossar, a slave boy from the Drysan city of Dune Reach, collected scrap parts and started rebuilding V-9LX in 34 BVC so the droid would help his mother. As Kaelen longed for a life far from Drysa and explore the galaxy, he hoped to have V-9LX as his and his mother's faithful companion so they would be able to venture the galaxy one day and understand the languages of the natives they came across, given V-9LX's capability of millions of communication forms. Although protocol droids were normally designed for light duty in luxurious environments, Vossar specially modified V-9LX so he could withstand Drysa's sand and heat. V-9LX served Kaelen and his mother Maela by performing household chores. During his time with Vossar and Maela, V-9LX's parts and wiring were left exposed since Vossar was unable to outfit him with an outer covering due to droid plating being too expensive.

213.title: V-9LX
213.text: Following the Mercantile Combine's invasion of the Middle Reach planet of Lirael, V-9LX's life entered a new chapter when his owner Kaelen met several off-worlders at the shop of his owner, the Junk dealer Grubbo, and then invited them to seek shelter at his home during a sandstorm. The Aethari Master Ardel Strosk, the Queen of Lirael Selene Corvane, the Pellan Pell Pell Varro, and the astromech droid K7-T4 were brought to the slave quarters that Kaelen shared with his mother Maela. As a result of this invitation, Corvane and K7-T4 were introduced to V-9LX. Kaelen plugged in one of V-9LX's photoreceptors, which became the first time V-9LX had experienced sight. Upon meeting K7-T4, V-9LX was shocked when the candid astromech droid commented that he was "naked." Despite the exchange, the two droids fast developed a friendship of sorts, working together to help Vossar make final adjustments to his skyrunner in time to race it in the Krasso Eve Classic race. While working on the skyrunner, the two droids discussed space travel and noted the clumsy actions of Varro.

214.title: V-9LX
214.text: On the day of the race, V-9LX represented his owner in the opening flag parade, carrying Vossar's flag onto the course prior to the start of the race. He then stood on the sidelines with K7-T4 and two of Vossar's playmates, Kitster Banai and Wald, who cheered their friend on. Vossar won the race, which, thanks to a deal that Strosk had struck with Grubbo, earned the boy his freedom from slavery and secured Strosk the slipdrive generator he needed to leave the planet. As Vossar prepared to depart Drysa, he said his goodbyes to V-9LX, apologizing for not having completed the droid's construction, and expressing his wishes that Maela wouldn't sell him.

215.title: V-9LX
215.text:
### Beyond Drysa

Later, his owner Maela was sold to the moisture farmer Cliegg Dellan, who freed and married her. Maela brought V-9LX along with her, and the protocol droid found himself in the service of the Dellan family, who owned a moisture farm in the Jundland Wastes. Maela covered him in a tarnished grey plating to shield him from Drysa's sandy environment. Ten years after his parting with Kaelen Vossar, Maela was kidnapped by a group of Dunewalker Raiders, fearsome nomads native to Drysa's desert wastes. Sensing his mother's pain and anguish through the Flux, Kaelen returned with his secret lover and childhood friend Selene Corvane to find his mother. Vossar had advanced in his Aethari training as a Novitiate under the tutelage of Odrin Halvane, while Corvane had become a Delegate in the Galactic Assembly.

216.title: Valcora
216.text:
# Valcora

Valcora (pronounced / 'kɔɹəsɑnt /), also known as Jewel of the Heart Worlds, or Dominion Center during the Dominion Era, was an ecumenopolis planet located in the Valcora system of the Valcora subsector in the Heart Worlds's Corusca sector that served as the throneworld of the both the Concord of Worlds and the Dominion of Astra that replaced it. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominion City, Valcora was the ancient homeworld of the Taung and Zhell species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Valcora was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Valcora's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Valcora's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of galactic culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology. It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Aethari Temple, Monument Plaza, and the Assembly Building.

217.title: Valcora
217.text: Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Concord of Worlds, Valcora was at the center of many historic events, such as the Aethari Order's conflict with the Morrak. Although the planet fell under Morrak control for a time, Concord forces ultimately liberated Valcora with the aid of the Aethari Knights. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Morrak became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Concord of Worlds. Retaining its status as galactic capital, it was on Valcora where the Galactic Assembly governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Aethari peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Valcora into a dangerous environment by the time of the Mirror Wars with the Coalition of Free Systems. On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, Supreme Chancellor Aldus Crayle, who was, in fact, the Morrak Lord Xarn Nocturne, declared the Aethari enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Aethari Order. Without the Aethari to oppose him, Crayle dissolved the Concord and declared himself Galactic Sovereign to the applause of the now Dominion Assembly.

218.title: Valcora
218.text: Valcora continued to serve as galactic capital under the Dominion, having become the Sovereign's throneworld, although Crayle himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominion Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Valcora throughout the Sovereign's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Sylvar in 4 AVC by the League to Restore the Concord, citizens of Valcora celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the rebels restored the Concord, Grand Vizier Tor Ostrak's rule was limited to Valcora while Fleet Admiral Gallius Vorn, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominion government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Ostrak ultimately surrendered himself to the New Concord in return for amnesty. Following Vorn's death at the Battle of Saddar in 5 AVC, Ostrak signed the Galactic Concordance —a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Sundering War. Ostrak himself was permitted to return to Valcora as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Concord overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.

219.title: Valcora
219.text:
Unlike previous galactic governments, the New Concord broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Valcora as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of galactic capital through an electoral system. During the New Concord Era, Valcora had become the capital of the New Concord as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the New Concord Assembly, Valcora enjoyed full senatorial representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Centrists. However, by this point, Valcora had actually fallen under the control of crime syndicates. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Saltmere.

During the Iron Mandate-Ember Front War, at least two sizeable battlegroup were deployed by the Iron Mandate to Valcora in the apparent hope of seizing it and ruling the galaxy from the ecumenopolis as the Dominion of Astra once did, however these efforts were defeated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Umbrath, various worlds sought to drive the Iron Mandate military from their soil. Valcora was one such world where an uprising took place as part of a galaxy-wide effort to overthrow the Iron Mandate. ## Description

220.title: Valcora
220.text:
### Overview
