Valcora, also known as Dominion Center during the Dominion Era or as the Jewel of the Heart Worlds, was an ecumenopolis Planet located within the Valcora system in the Valcora subsector of the Corusca sector in an intersecting portion of the Heart Worlds and The Interior. The homeworld of the Zhell and Taung species and widely accepted as the origin point of humans, Valcora, located in grid square L-9 of the Standard Galactic Grid, was situated at the junction between many vital and important slipspace routes including the Dravosi Run, the Koros Trunk Line, the Metellos Trade Route, the Namadii Corridor, the Perlemian Trade Route, the Stassia Alley, and the secret Nexus Route, served as the throneworld of multiple Galactic Governments, first for the Concord of Worlds, then for it's successor state, the Dominion of Astra, and even briefly for the New Concord in 9 AVC, leading to the planet gaining the coordinates 0, 0, 0 despite not being in the actual Center of The galaxy. Due to Courscant's importance in galactic history, even later governments such as the Iron Mandate would even attempt to conquer the planet and make it their capital, though their efforts would ultimately fail.

221.title: Valcora
221.text: Valcora had four moons — Centax-1, Centax-2, Centax-3, and Hesperidium. Valcora orbited Valcora Prime, the only star of the Valcora system, with an orbital period of 365 Local days, with each day lasting 24 Standard hours. The Valcora week lasted five days, with each days with the name of each day relating to Valcora is some way— Primeday, named after Valcora's sun, Centaxday, named after Valcora's primary moon, Taungsday, named after the native Taung species, Zhellday, named after the native Zhell species, and Benduday, named after the Dai Bendu monks from Valcora. When the need for a standardized time system between worlds arose in the Galaxy, the Galactic Standard Calendar was created, which standardized days and years to Valcora's orbital period and rotational period respectively.

222.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
222.text:
# VC-1 Orbital Battle Station

The VC-1 Orbital Battle Station, also designated as the VC-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, referred to as the Ultimate Weapon in early development stages, later known as the Void Core I or the First Void Core, often simply referred to as the Void Core, and codenamed Ashfall, was a moon-sized, deep- space mobile battle station constructed by the Dominion of Astra. It had been designed to fire a single planet-destroying superlaser focused by massive aurite crystals which would destroy any planet targeted. It was the pet project of Sovereign Crayle, Director Edric Callan Varsh, and its eventual commander Grand Prefect Corvin Vessic to expound the military philosophy of the aptly named Vessic Doctrine.

Some of the earliest plans for a mobile, planet-destroying superweapon dated back millennia to the ancient Morrak. Thousands of years later, shortly before the outbreak of the Mirror Wars, the Karrikans, aligned with Count Varkon and the Coalition of Free Systems, designed the Ultimate Weapon in secret. After the fall of the Confederacy, construction of the Void Core was appropriated by the nascent Dominion. It was built in orbit of Karrik and supported by a complex logistical network of bases. The station, which took many years longer to complete than expected, was eventually moved from Karrik to Corall in its final stages of construction.

223.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
223.text:
The Axis network learned of the battle station's existence in a breach of Dominion Security Bureau files, and passed the knowledge through several operatives until it reached the League to Restore the Concord at their secret base on Ostara IV. Though the League was initially skeptical of the intel and its source, an unrelated Insurgent spy soon corroborated enough of the information for the Insurgents to begin an investigation. Division emerged within League leadership; some believed such a weapon too great a threat to justify continued insurrection and resistance, while others believed the Void Core was too great a threat to ignore, and must be destroyed. Ultimately, rogue operatives Mira Halden and Dorin Sorrel led a mission, which the Free League soon joined, to steal the battle station's design plans, as Halden had discovered that her father, who had been the primary engineer behind the station’s superweapon, had left a fatal flaw in the design, which could enable the Void Core to be destroyed with relative ease.

Having retrieved the Void Core plans from the Dominion Center of Military Research on Corall, Halden was able to transmit them to the Insurgent fleet above the planet, and they were received by Princess Ilsa Marrow of Seravel aboard the Valiant IV. Ilsa then fled through slipspace toward Drysa, where she was apprehended by Xarn Velgor, but not before having hidden the plans in her astromech K7-T4. While the Princess was taken prisoner, her droid was able to escape and bring the plans to Odrin Halvane, a former Aethari Knight living in hiding on Drysa.

224.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
224.text:
In an attempt to coerce Ilsa, now held captive on the battle station itself, into revealing the location of the Free League's secret base, Governor Vessic ordered the first full test of the Void Core, destroying the Princess' home planet of Seravel. Shortly thereafter Ilsa managed to escape captivity on the Void Core with the help of Odrin Halvane and Tavin Vossar, who had been brought to Seravel by pilots Dace Rennick and Grawlok in an effort to reunite the recovered Void Core plans to Ilsa's father and Free League leader, Corran Marrow.

Ilsa brought the plans to the League leadership on Ostara IV, who quickly analyzed the data and discovered the design flaw deliberately left in the battle station by Dominion engineer Orrin Halden, which would allow a single proton torpedo, fired into the thermal exhaust port, to destroy the entire station. The League launched a small assault against the Void Core, which had followed the escaping rebels to the Ostara system. The original Void Core was destroyed moments before opening fire on the moon by a shot fired by Insurgent pilot Tavin Vossar with the aid of the Flux. While Xarn Velgor escaped, due to having joined the dogfight above the station in his Rak fighter, many high-ranking Dominion officers perished aboard the space station, including Corvin Vessic, Wullf Yularen, and Conan Motti.

225.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
225.text: The destruction of the Void Core weakened the Dominion Military, and Insurgent assaults on Dominion installations prompted the construction of a second Void Core, both as a sign of defiance and technological terror. Despite this, it, like its predecessor, was destroyed with all hands lost. Decades later, the Dominion's successor state, the Iron Mandate, constructed Sunreaver Base, a much larger planet-destroying superweapon considered to be an evolution of the Void Core project of the Old Dominion. ## Description

226.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
226.text:
### Overall design

The station was spheroid, and measured 160 km (100 miles) in diameter with 357 internal levels and a surface area of over 45,000 square kilometers. A large, concave dish in the northern hemisphere made up the superlaser emitter. The station's command bridge, the Overbridge, was located above the dish of the station's superlaser, within the Northern Polar Command Sector. The war room featured designated posts for Vessic and other officers, a HoloNet booth for communicating with the Sovereign, and large banks of viewscreens. Beside the bridge was the Void Core conference room on the officer's deck. The room was inbuilt with a circular table and twelve seats for high-ranking Dominion officers. The Sovereign's tower and its throne room also fell within the Command Sector.

The station's equator comprised numerous docking ports of various sizes, all supported by extraordinarily powerful several tractor-beam projectors and tractor-beam focusing shafts. The station's equator housed docking and hangar bays, tractor-beam generators, projectors, and emitter towers, turbolaser emplacements, and mooring platforms for ships of the fleet, including Dominion-class Dreadhulls. "Tulip" style Dominion work stations were located throughout the station in different rooms.

227.title: VC-1 Orbital Battle Station
227.text:
A habitable crust several kilometers thick was composed of command centers, armories, maintenance blocks, and other requirements for a fully operational space station. Unused stories in the station's lower levels held backup weapons operators in the event of an emergency. Levels in the station's southern hemisphere extended downward through armories, deep storage, and a southern command sector. Massive girders provided grid-like support to the lower levels. Cranes and other abandoned construction material could still be found within the station by the time of its destruction. With the exception of the crust, the station's entire interior space was uninhabited, and housed the hypermatter reactor, slipdrive, 123 Kuat Drive Yards sublight engines, and the station's superweapon. The station's outer hull was made of quadanium steel plates.

Several modular artificial atmosphere stations and water-recycling tanks were dotted throughout the station's levels for the creation of air and humidity. Several large, cavernous airways served as means for circulation and as an emergency air dump in case of atmosphere contamination. A large, central airway existed for each sector. Magnetic seals and an atmosphere-containment projector kept the station's internal atmosphere in and the vacuum of space out if docking-bay doors were opened.

228.title: Xarn Nocturne
228.text:
# Xarn Nocturne

Xarn Nocturne, born Aldus Crayle and also simply known as the Sovereign, was a human male Dark Lord of the Morrak and Sovereign of the Dominion of Astra, with his reign lasting from 19 BVC to 4 AVC. Rising to power in the Galactic Assembly as the delegate of Lirael, the secretive Morrak Lord cultivated two identities, Nocturne and Crayle, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Concord of Worlds and the Aethari Order through the Mirror Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Sylvar. However, the dark side of the Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Sovereign was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Umbrath by Nira, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast replicant son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.

229.title: Xarn Nocturne
229.text: Born on the Middle Reach planet Lirael in 84 BVC, Aldus Crayle possessed a strong connection to the Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Morrak by Xarn Morvex with Crayle taking Xarn Nocturne as his Morrak persona. He eventually betrayed and killed his Morrak Master, in order to train his own Morrak apprentice, Xarn Skarr, for the Law of Pairs limited their ranks to two Morrak Lords at any given time. The Invasion of Lirael, a crisis orchestrated by Nocturne, led to the Assembly to elect Crayle as Supreme Chancellor, although this came at the loss of Skarr, who was defeated and presumed killed in the Battle of Lirael. The Secessionist Crisis and the Mirror Wars were masterminded by Nocturne and his second apprentice, Xarn Vexus, in an effort to achieve galactic dominance. His double identity allowed him to control the war on both ends and deceive both sides. Following an attempt to arrest the chancellor, the Great Aethari Purge commenced with Nocturne enacting Directive Nine.

230.title: Xarn Nocturne
230.text: With the Aethari all but extinct, Nocturne installed the New Order in the Concord's place, declaring himself Galactic Sovereign and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Vexus, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Aethari Knight Kaelen Vossar to the dark side and transforming him into Xarn Velgor. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the League to Restore the Concord. During the Sundering War, the Sovereign sought to betray Velgor, by replacing him with the latter's son, Tavin Vossar. However, Nocturne' plan backfired when Velgor ultimately renounced the dark side and killed Nocturne to protect Tavin. Thus, with the Morrak's destruction, the Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Kaelen's destiny as the prophesied Foretold One.

231.title: Xarn Nocturne
231.text: Through his master's teachings, however, Nocturne transferred his essence to an imperfect replicant vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Contingency to destroy the Dominion of Astra and replace it with a new Morrak Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the New Concord and the emergence of the Iron Mandate, the creation of Supreme Leader Gorrath, who turned Corin Rennick —heir to the Vossar bloodline —to the dark side, and the establishment of the Last Mandate. When the Sovereign announced his return to the galaxy in 35 AVC, the Ember Front invaded the planet Umbrath, Nocturne' hidden stronghold in the Uncharted Expanse. During the battle, the resurrected Sovereign discovered a dyad in the Flux in the form of the bond between Rennick and Nira, a Novitiate sired from the Crayle bloodline. His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Nira called upon the strength of past Aethari to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Nocturne and his Morrak Eternal cultists. ## Biography

232.title: Xarn Nocturne
232.text:
### Early life and apprenticeship

The origins of Xarn Nocturne were closely guarded secrets that he took to his grave more than once. He was born on the Middle Reach planet Lirael as Aldus Crayle, eighty-four years before the Battle of Ostara. The dynastic, noble Crayle family belonged to the affluent class in Lirael society, although throughout several points of time of his life, Crayle did not have any living family members as far as the public was aware, and no records of obituaries for his parents existed, marking him as the last of his ancient family bloodline. Crayle was raised in the cultured city of Elmira, his homeworld's capital; he formed connections with a reputable host of credible politicians produced over the centuries, all the while acquiring a great amount of knowledge on governance and the subtleties of power during his youth. As such, Crayle had been skilled in manipulation since boyhood.

The details about how Nocturne came to study under the Morrak were known by very few, with it not even being known of when he did, but he became the Morrak apprentice to Dark Lord of the Morrak Xarn Morvex and took on the name Xarn Nocturne by 52 BVC. As a Morrak Lord, Nocturne learned all his Morrak Master knew about the dark side of the Flux, following the tradition first set by the ancient Xarn Kesh. While apprenticed to Morvex, Nocturne constructed his own Morrak lumeblades. At the same time, little by little, he began to secure political power.

233.title: Xarn Nocturne
233.text: As a young man, Crayle had traveled throughout the galaxy, collecting art, at least some of which was connected to the dark side, while doing so. Unaware docents would have written off his collection as junk, but Crayle knew better. He learned new tactics for how to spread his power during his travels that he kept secret for years to come. While training with Morvex, Nocturne was taught that two Morrak were required for their perilous machinations. So, if they worked together in accordance to Xarn Kesh's Law of Pairs, with one of them serving as bait for the dark side of the Flux and the other as a vessel, they would succeed in acquiring the ability to harness the full power of the dark side and rule immortal for ten thousand years.

234.title: Xarn Nocturne
234.text: Xarn Nocturne and Xarn Morvex worked together for years, trying to unlock the secrets to immortality, which was the obsession and longtime lust of Morvex. Nocturne was eventually made aware of Morvex' ability to manipulate the lumicytes to create life, which his master employed to prevent the people he cared for from dying. Morvex believed the secret to immortality laid within science, and so conducted "unnatural" experiments with his rare ability to manipulate the lumicytes, as part of the pair's in depth studies into the biological underpinnings of life itself. Though they were incomplete, they were encouraging to Nocturne. According to Xarn Nocturne' book, The Secrets of the Morrak, written later on his life, Morvex discovered a form of "immortality" through transference, a Flux power that allowed the user to transfer their spirit and consciousness to another body, essentially using bodies as vessels. This obsession with extending one's own life later passed onto Nocturne from his time as Galactic Sovereign. Morvex also attempted to create a Flux dyad with Nocturne, a unique Flux-bond as strong as life itself and which was predecessor to the Law of Pairs. However, Morvex was unable to form the dyad.
